notes: Swift URL(string:) is replaced by java.net.URI wrapped in runCatching, so a parse failure yields null just like the Swift optional initialiser.
Swift's url.port == nil maps to URI.port == -1, since java.net.URI uses -1 for a missing port.
url.host() maps to URI.host, which is null for strings without an authority component.
The URLComponents(url:resolvingAgainstBaseURL:) sanity check is kept as a second URI parse so the control flow and returned message stay the same.
Int32(value) maps to toIntOrNull(): Kotlin Int has the same 32-bit range, so overflow behaviour is identical.
UInt(value) maps to toUIntOrNull() and UInt16.max to UShort.MAX_VALUE.toUInt().
makeRtmpUri and makeRtmpStreamKey are assumed to live in com.moblin.android.common.various and are called unqualified; adjust the import if they are in another package.
localized comes from com.moblin.android; the interpolated 'Unsupported scheme' and 'Only ... allowed' strings keep the Swift wording.

Swift's synthesised Codable for enums with associated values uses the externally tagged form {"case":{...}}, so each sealed class gets a hand-written KSerializer that reproduces that exact JSON, including {} for payload-less cases.
MoblinkResult has no raw values in Swift but is Codable, so it encodes as {"ok":{}}; it is an enum class with rawValue/fromRawValue plus MoblinkResultSerializer producing that single-key object.
moblinkJson uses explicitNulls = false to match Swift's encodeIfPresent, so nil batteryPercentage/thermalState/data keys are omitted instead of written as null.
Optional payload fields get Kotlin default null so a missing key decodes like Swift's decodeIfPresent.
Swift JSONEncoder writes UUID as an uppercase string; MoblinkUuidSerializer reproduces that and accepts any case when decoding.
UInt16 port is translated to UShort per the wire-format rule; kotlinx.serialization serialises it as a plain unsigned JSON number.

The Swift 'Not a UTF-8 string' / 'Encode failed' guards disappear: Kotlin Strings are already decodable, so fromJson just throws SerializationException on bad input and toJson() on MoblinkMessageToRelay still returns null via runCatching.
Sealed subclass names are capitalised (StartTunnel, Status, Hello, ...) but the JSON keys stay byte-identical to the Swift case names.
[[UInt8]] maps to MutableList<UByteArray>: the 2D grayscale buffer stays byte-oriented and mutates in place like the Swift arrays.
UByte comparisons need toInt() (UByte has no compareTo(Int)), so pixel reads are widened where arithmetic happens.
Swift's ternary threshold becomes a Kotlin if/else; newColor stays Int so the diff arithmetic is unchanged.
Int division by 8 keeps Kotlin's truncate-toward-zero semantics, matching Swift for negative diffs.
guard with multiple conditions becomes an early return with a negated conjunction, preserving the exact bounds check.
min/max clamping becomes coerceIn(0, 255) before converting back with toUByte().
The instance keeps the same mutable state fields (image, width, height) and the same apply/adjustPixel call order.
No Apple frameworks are used, so there is nothing unsupported.
Swift's `extension Bool { var uint8: UInt8 }` becomes a top-level extension property `val Boolean.uint8: UByte` in this file.
UInt8 maps to UByte; Kotlin has no UByte literal syntax, so the values are written as `1u.toUByte()` and `0u.toUByte()`.
The property is a getter-only computed property, matching the Swift read-only computed property.
Swift extends the ExpressibleByIntegerLiteral protocol; Kotlin has no such common supertype for primitives, so `data` is declared once per integer type instead.
Memory layout in Swift's withUnsafeBytes is native byte order, which is little-endian on both Apple and Android platforms; java.nio.ByteBuffer.LITTLE_ENDIAN reproduces it exactly.
Byte.data is a direct byteArrayOf(this) because a single byte needs no buffer.
Unsigned types (UByte/UShort/UInt/ULong) are included so call sites using unsigned literals still compile; UByte reuses the Byte path.
Extension properties are top-level in the file, matching the Swift extension in a separate file.
No top-level types are declared here, only extension properties, so declared_types is empty.
UShort is used for the UInt16 revolution and time fields since these are ANT/CPS wire-format values.
ContinuousClock.Instant maps to java.time.Instant and ContinuousClock.now to Instant.now() at construction time.
duration(to:) is translated as Duration.between(latestAverageCadenceUpdateTime, now) compared with Duration.ofSeconds(3).
The top-level averageSampleCount constant stays a private top-level const val.
DoubleArray replaces the Swift Array<Double> for fixed-size sample storage.
min(cadence, 10000) becomes minOf(cadence, 10000.0).
Swift's shadowing 'if let revolutions, let time' is expressed with explicit null checks and local vals.
averageIgnoreZeros keeps the same zero-filtering and divide-by-count behaviour, returning 0.0 for an empty set.
Swift struct with mutating methods becomes a Kotlin class so counters can be mutated in place.
The (Int, Int)? tuple return becomes Pair<Int, Int>?, keeping the same field order (duplicated, dropped).
The Swift `defer` block that zeroes both counters is expressed by snapshotting the counters into a local Pair before resetting them and returning it.
`private static let outputInterval` becomes a private const in the companion object.
Comparison logic was inverted into early returns to mirror the two `guard` statements.
Since this is pure logic with no Apple frameworks, unsupported is empty.
Pixel bytes stay UByte (matching Swift's UInt8) inside MutableList<MutableList<UByte>>; every arithmetic step converts with toInt() first because Kotlin has no implicit unsigned promotion.
The threshold test uses this.image[y][x].toInt() > 127 instead of comparing a UByte with an unsigned literal, avoiding cross-width unsigned comparison ambiguity.
Swift's value semantics are preserved by copying the incoming rows into fresh MutableLists, so the caller's array is not mutated.
Integer division (diff * 7 / 16 etc.) truncates toward zero in both languages, so the error diffusion weights are byte-identical.
clamping uses coerceIn(0, 255).toUByte(), the equivalent of Swift's UInt8(min(255, max(0, value))).
The private state (image, width, height) is kept exactly as in Swift so instances can be reused exactly like the original.
The method name apply is retained for side-by-side reading; it resolves to the member function because the stdlib scope function apply requires a lambda argument.
AVCaptureColorSpace is an AVFoundation type with no Android counterpart, so it is declared in this file as an enum class that keeps the Swift case names, raw values and a companion fromRawValue.
The Swift `description` computed property in the extension becomes a top-level Kotlin extension property on AVCaptureColorSpace in this same package.
CustomStringConvertible has no Kotlin equivalent; toString() is overridden on the enum to delegate to description so string interpolation matches Swift.
Raw values follow AVFoundation (sRGB = 1, P3_D65 = 2, HLG_BT2020 = 3, appleLog = 4); verify against the platform header if these numbers are ever persisted or sent over the wire.
The Swift `default:` branch is kept as `else -> "Unknown"` so values that do not map to a known case keep the same output.
If another Moblin module already declares AVCaptureColorSpace, remove the declaration here and import that one instead.
Kotlin enums are closed, so unknown platform values can only be represented by a null return from fromRawValue or by the else branch of description.
Swift's `Any` maps to Kotlin's `Any?`; the parameter is nullable so callers can pass anything.
Swift `Int` is 64-bit while Kotlin `Int` is 32-bit, so a boxed `Long` value will not match the `is Int` branch; use `Long` at call sites only if that parity is required.
The value is matched with Kotlin `is` checks, which correspond exactly to Swift's conditional `as?` casts, including falling through to `false` for any other type.
No Android or Apple frameworks are used, so the translation is complete and compiles as-is.
CoreAudio is not available on Android, so the `AudioStreamBasicDescription` struct itself is declared here as a Kotlin `data class` with the nine fields used by the Swift extension.

The Swift extension only adds `Equatable`; in Kotlin the data class generates `equals`/`hashCode` over exactly the same nine properties, so the `==` implementation is reproduced without an explicit operator.

Fields are mutable (`var`) to mirror the mutability of the imported Swift C struct, and are declared in the canonical CoreAudio order (`mSampleRate`, `mFormatID`, `mFormatFlags`, `mBytesPerPacket`, `mFramesPerPacket`, `mBytesPerFrame`, `mChannelsPerFrame`, `mBitsPerChannel`, `mReserved`).
The `UInt32` fields are mapped to Kotlin `UInt` because an audio stream format description is wire-format/byte-parsing data, and `mSampleRate` (`Float64`) is mapped to `Double`.
All fields are defaulted to `0u`/`0.0` so a zeroed format description can be built without arguments, matching C's zero-initialised struct.
No `CoreAudio` symbol remains to be stubbed, so no `TODO()` and no unsupported entries are needed.
BitrateStatsInstant is a plain value holder, so it becomes a data class with ULong properties like the Swift UInt64 ones.
BitrateStats mutates its own stored state, so it is translated as a Kotlin class instead of a data class; no copy-on-write value semantics are needed by the algorithm.
private(set) members become public properties with a private setter (totalBytes and latestSpeed).
Swift's default parameter value 100 becomes the ULong default 100uL on the constructor.
add(bytesTransferred:) converts the Int argument with toULong() before adding it to the running total.
The subtraction (100 - speedChangeRate) is kept as unsigned ULong arithmetic, matching the Swift expression exactly.
The smoothing formula uses the same multiplication/addition/division-by-100 ordering as Swift, so results are bit-identical.
The mutating funcs become regular member functions and return BitrateStatsInstant directly, as in the Swift source.
Swift UInt32 bitrate values became Int: this port reserves UByte/UShort/UInt/ULong for wire-format code, and bitrates are never negative.
`weak let delegate` has no Kotlin equivalent; it is stored as a plain nullable reference, so the delegate is not weakly held.
ContinuousClock.Instant mapped to monotonic System.nanoTime() nanoseconds (type Long) so the 15 second expiry test is immune to wall-clock jumps.
swift-collections Deque mapped to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque (firstOrNull peek, addLast, removeFirst).
DateFormatter mapped to java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter with the system default zone, formatting an Instant.
logger.debug mapped to android.util.Log.d with tag "AdaptiveBitrate".
The Swift method-name typo logAdaptiveAcion is preserved verbatim so both codebases read side by side.
limitByTransportBitrate keeps Swift's integer arithmetic (17 * transportBitrate) / 10 using maxOf/minOf on Long.
The caseless Swift `enum AudioSpecificConfig` used only as a namespace becomes a Kotlin `object` holding three nested `enum class` types, preserving the nesting and declaration order.
UInt8 raw values are mapped to UByte (MPEG-4 ASC values are byte-level wire data); literal values use the `u` suffix.
Each enum gets a `companion object` with `fromRawValue(value: UByte)` to mirror the `init?(rawValue:)` initializer Swift synthesizes for raw-value enums.

Enum case names are kept byte-identical to the Swift names (lowerCamelCase, e.g. `aacLc`, `hz44100`, `frontLeftAndFrontRight`) so the two codebases can be read side by side instead of being renamed to SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.
`SamplingFrequency.sampleRate` (Float64) becomes a computed `val sampleRate: Double` implemented with a `when (this)` expression; the values and their order match the Swift switch.
No imports are required; the file only declares nested enums and one numeric mapping.
No Apple platform frameworks are used, so nothing needed a TODO().
Data is mapped to ByteArray; the private(set) setters become Kotlin 'private set'.
top-level 'let nalUnitEmulationPreventionByte' becomes a top-level const val of type UByte to stay in wire-format semantics.
UInt8 bit-write APIs use UByte and UInt32 uses UInt, matching the wire-format mapping rules.
Swift Data.insert(at:) has no ByteArray counterpart, so insertEmulationPreventionByteIfNeeded reallocates the buffer and copies both segments with ByteArray.copyInto.
Swift '|=' on a Data byte is expressed as an explicit toInt() or mask then toByte().
The emulation-prevention toggle is kept as a private val field declared after data/bitOffset to preserve the Swift declaration order.
writeRawBytes keeps 'self.data += data' as an explicit this.data = this.data + data assignment.
URL extension becomes a java.net.URI extension because this file parses URL components, not a stored string.

absoluteWithoutAuthenticationString rebuilds the URI with the 7-argument java.net.URI constructor passing a null userInfo, which drops both user and password; java.net.URISyntaxException is caught with runCatching.
When the URI has no user info the original toString() is returned verbatim, so URIs are not needlessly re-normalised.
dictionaryFromQuery works on rawQuery and percent-decodes names and values itself; the '+' character is kept literal, matching Foundation's URLComponents.
Query items without '=' are skipped, matching the Swift `if let value` check.
The helper percentDecode is a private top-level function used only by dictionaryFromQuery.
Malformed percent escapes are decoded leniently instead of yielding an empty map as URLComponents would.
File-scope `let defaultStunServer` becomes a top-level `const val defaultStunServer` with the identical name and value.
`setupWebrtcDebugLogging()` keeps its signature but its body only calls `rtcInitLogger`, which comes from the libdatachannel C library; no Kotlin binding exists in this port, so the body is a TODO().
The debug-log callback would have been translated to `android.util.Log.i` with the class name as tag, but it is unreachable because the registration call is a TODO().
No Apple-only framework is used here; the only missing piece is the native WebRTC logger bridge.
When a JNI wrapper for libdatachannel is added, `setupWebrtcDebugLogging()` should register a callback that forwards the C string to `Log.i("WebrtcCommon", "webrtc: $message")`.
unsupported: libdatachannel `rtcInitLogger` / `RTC_LOG_DEBUG` (C library, no Android binding in this port)

notes: Two top-level Swift functions become top-level Kotlin functions in com.moblin.android.streamingplatforms.twitch.
The Swift switch with implicit case values becomes a Kotlin `when` expression returning Int, with the same 1/2/3/default mapping.
The Swift tuple (moving:still:) has no Kotlin equivalent, so it is modelled by a small data class TwitchEmoteUrls with properties in the same order.
URL is translated to String because these URLs are only built and passed on for image loading, never parsed.
The Swift optional return survives a failing URL(string:) call; Kotlin string concatenation cannot fail, so the nullable return type is kept only for call-site fidelity.
No Apple framework is used, so the unsupported list is empty.
Crc32 remains a class with a private constructor and a companion object holding the single `mpeg2` instance, mirroring Swift's `static let mpeg2`.
Swift `Data` becomes `ByteArray`; CRC arithmetic keeps unsigned semantics with `UInt`/`UIntArray` since this is wire-format bit math.
Kotlin's infix bitwise functions (`and`, `shl`, `xor`) are all left-associative and bind looser than `==`, so the Swift expressions were parenthesised to keep the exact same evaluation order.
The Swift constructor parameter `polynomial` is kept as a constructor parameter, not a property, and is only used while building the lookup table.
The table build loop, the 0xFFFFFFFF seed and the byte-sequential update loop are translated literally, including the wrap-around `shl 24` for indices 128..255.
`data[i].toUInt() and 0xFFu` reproduces Swift's `UInt32(data[i]) & 0xFF`, so negative bytes cannot sign-extend into the index.
No Apple platform framework is used in this file, so nothing is stubbed with TODO().
@MainActor is translated to a CoroutineScope bound to Dispatchers.Main, so both handlers run on the main thread exactly like the main-queue DispatchSourceTimer in Swift.

DispatchSourceTimer single-shot and repeating schedules become coroutine Jobs driven by delay(): the single shot delays 'timeout' then runs, the periodic timer delays 'initial ?? interval', runs, then loops with 'interval' delays.
Double seconds are converted to Long milliseconds for delay(); sub-millisecond precision is lost.

The Swift 'isolated deinit { stop() }' has no deterministic Kotlin counterpart because Kotlin objects are not deinitialized eagerly; callers must call stop() (the timer Job keeps the scope alive otherwise).
The stored 'timer' property keeps its Swift name and now holds a Job? instead of an optional DispatchSourceTimer.
stop() cancels the Job and resets the property to null, matching timer?.cancel(); timer = nil.
The 'initial: Double? = nil' optional parameter is preserved as a Kotlin nullable parameter with a default value.
The `handler` closure becomes a nullable `(String) -> Unit` property; call it with `handler?.invoke(line)`.
The `@autoclosure` parameter of `debug` is translated to a `() -> String` lambda so the message is only evaluated when `debugEnabled` is true.
Swift's `DateFormatter` is replaced by a thread-safe `java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter` held in the companion object; `Instant.now()` is converted with the system default zone before formatting.

The compile-time `#if DEBUG` print is replaced by an unconditional `android.util.Log.d` with tag `EasyLogger`; R8/ProGuard or a `BuildConfig.DEBUG` check can be added if release stripping is required.
The global `nonisolated(unsafe) let logger` becomes a top-level `val logger`, initialised once when the file's class is loaded.
`makeTimestamp` and `log` stay `private` instance members and the timestamp prefix format `HH:mm:ss.SSS` is preserved byte-for-byte.
`nonisolated(unsafe)` has no Kotlin counterpart; the singleton is a plain top-level property whose mutable state is not synchronised (same as the Swift original).
Swift enums used purely as namespaces of static constants become Kotlin objects.
UInt16 port constants are translated to Int (const val) because java.net Socket/ServerSocket/DatagramSocket APIs take Int ports and the values fit comfortably.
Values are compile-time constants so they use const val, mirroring Swift 'static let' semantics.
Names and declaration order are preserved exactly for side-by-side reading.
No Apple frameworks, so the unsupported list is empty.
OSAllocatedUnfairLock has no Android counterpart and is replaced by java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock (non-fair, like the Swift lock) used through kotlin.concurrent.withLock.
The Swift Sendable constraints are dropped: Kotlin generics are unconstrained, so Atomic<A> and mutate<R> are plain generics.
Swift's inout A cannot be expressed in Kotlin, so mutate hands the transform a nested mutable holder MutableRef<A>; callers read and write ref.value instead of using $0.
Atomic is a class rather than a data class because instances own a lock and mutable state; value semantics would copy the lock.
value stays a read-only property whose getter reads the state under the lock, mirroring Swift's computed var.
mutate executes the transform while holding the lock and returns R unchanged; the primary constructor parameter is named initialValue to avoid shadowing the value property.
Call sites such as atomic.mutate { $0.count += 1 } become atomic.mutate { it.value.count += 1 }.
No Apple-only framework is used, so the unsupported list is empty.
Swift Data becomes ByteArray; the private(set) data property stays publicly readable but is mutated through local copies, matching Swift value semantics.
UInt8/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64 map to UByte/UShort/UInt/ULong because this is wire-format byte handling; Int32 maps to Int.
The Data.bigEndian.data and Double.data.reversed() extensions from the HaishinKit extensions file are inlined with java.nio.ByteBuffer using BIG_ENDIAN order.
writeBytes(UnsafeRawBufferPointer) is translated to an overload taking java.nio.ByteBuffer, consuming its remaining bytes via duplicate() so the caller's position is untouched.
In sequence(_:lambda:) the trailing `data.advanced(by: data.endIndex - r)` is treated as the remainder slice data[count-r ..< count] and wrapped in a new ByteWriter.
UInt32(data:) used by toUInt32() is reimplemented inline reading 4 bytes big-endian from the region starting at position.
Both Swift initialisers are kept as Kotlin secondary constructors.
The subscript is translated to operator get/set with UByte values, writing into the backing signed ByteArray.
Data maps to ByteArray and the private(set) var data becomes a var with a private setter; the Swift init(data:) becomes the primary constructor in the class header.
The private Swift.Error enum is translated to a private sealed class Error with the nested objects eof and utf8 so thrown failures keep the same names.

readUInt16 and readUInt32 no longer use the UnsafeRawBufferPointer helpers (which do not exist in Kotlin) and assemble the bytes explicitly big-endian, matching the high/low ordering of readUInt64 and the separate readUInt16Le/readUInt32Le variants.

readDouble keeps the Swift semantics verbatim: it consumes 8 bytes, reverses them and decodes them as a little-endian double, which is identical to decoding the untouched bytes big-endian as AMF0 requires.
defer { position += n } became an explicit increment placed after the read value has been captured.
readUtf8Bytes uses a strict UTF-8 decoder with CodingErrorAction.REPORT so malformed input throws Error.utf8 exactly like Swift's String(data:encoding:).
Unsigned wire values use UByte, UShort, UInt and ULong; callers outside this file therefore see Kotlin unsigned types.
skipBytes and readBytes keep the length >= 0 precondition and throw Error.eof on short buffers.
DispatchSourceTimer + DispatchQueue are replaced by a CoroutineScope backed by the given CoroutineDispatcher; the timer field holds the running Job.
Double seconds are converted to Long milliseconds for kotlinx.coroutines delay.
Swift's deinit calling stop() becomes AutoCloseable.close(), which calls stop(); callers should call close() when done.
The handler is a plain () -> Unit lambda; @Sendable has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped.
startPeriodic fires the first handler invocation after `initial ?: interval` and then repeats every interval, matching the Swift schedule.
startSingleShot and startPeriodic still call stop() first, so a previously running timer is always cancelled.

Swift's Data byte-reading extension methods (getUInt16Be/getUInt32Be) are not declared in this file and no shared byte-reader package was provided, so they are re-implemented here as file-private helpers readUInt16Be/readUInt32Be on ByteArray.
16-bit and 32-bit wire values are kept as UShort/UInt as prescribed for byte-parsing code; callers using the packet type should use SrtPacketType.fromRawValue(type).
packet[0] is a signed Byte in Kotlin, so the Swift UInt8 mask test became (packet[0].toInt() and 0x80) == 0.
SRT sequence numbers rely on wrapping unsigned arithmetic; Kotlin's UInt operators already wrap, so Swift's &- is no longer needed in processSrtNak.
SrtPacketType keeps the Swift lowerCamelCase entry names so both files can be read side by side; rawValue stays a UShort with identical raw values.
Swift's guard offset <= packet.count - 4 else { return } became an early return; the guard ... else { continue } became if (upToNakSn - fromNakSn >= 100_000u) continue.
The Swift closed range fromNakSn ... upToNakSn maps to fromNakSn..upToNakSn; a descending range is empty in Kotlin instead of trapping as it does in Swift (only reachable in a wrap-around edge case).
srtControlTypeSize is a const val Int and srtControlPacketTypeBit stays a top-level val UShort, matching the file-scope lets in Swift.
Keychain is backed by androidx.security:security-crypto EncryptedSharedPreferences (1.1.x) with a MasterKey using AES256_GCM; keys use AES256_SIV and values AES256_GCM.

The Swift version got the security context implicitly; here the application Context must be assigned to Keychain.appContext at app start, otherwise store/load/remove log and no-op and loadStreamIds returns an empty list.

Each server maps to its own encrypted preferences file named 'moblin_keychain_' + SHA-256 hex of the server, so that the static loadStreamIds(server) can enumerate all account names (streamIds) belonging to that server, like the kSecAttrServer query did.
Each streamId is the SharedPreferences key inside its server's file, matching kSecAttrAccount.

update/add use commit() instead of apply() so the Swift success/failure logging semantics are preserved; SharedPreferences has no separate update vs add, so update() only succeeds when the key already exists and store() falls back to add().
logger.info is replaced by android.util.Log.i with the tag "Keychain" (the class name).
The Swift guard on value.data(using: .utf8) is dropped since Kotlin String -> UTF-8 conversion cannot fail.
SharedPreferences files are cached per server in a synchronized map, and creation failures (GeneralSecurityException/IOException) are caught and logged like the original keychain status errors.
CMVideoDimensions is a CoreMedia struct with no Android counterpart, so it is mapped to android.util.Size; the Swift extension methods become top-level Kotlin extension functions on Size.
The @retroactive Equatable conformance needs no Kotlin code: android.util.Size already implements equals()/hashCode().
toSize() returns android.util.SizeF, the Float width/height analogue of CGSize (CoreGraphics CGFloat -> Float per the port rules).
convertTo(dimension:) keeps the Swift optional return type (Size?) and the odd-size rounding: the derived dimension is incremented when it is odd; it never actually returns null.
Int32 arithmetic maps to Kotlin Int; Swift traps on overflow while Kotlin wraps, which is unreachable for realistic video dimensions.
`public import AVFoundation` has no Kotlin equivalent; only android.util.Size and android.util.SizeF are imported.
Function names, parameter names and body order follow the Swift source; visibility is Kotlin's default public so other port files can call them.
ObservableObject with @Published became a private MutableStateFlow backing field plus a public read-only StateFlow named followUser / followHeading, matching the _name/name convention.

Because Swift hand-writes encode(to:) and init(from:) over @Published properties, the class uses @Serializable(with = SettingsNavigationSerializer::class) and a hand-written KSerializer that mirrors the Swift container encode/decode calls.
The Swift decoder defaults were false for both keys; deserialize() starts both locals at false so a missing key keeps the Swift behaviour.
The nested CodingKeys enum kept its name and nesting and stores the serialized key string in stringValue (the CodingKey.stringValue counterpart).
The Swift no-argument init() is preserved as a secondary constructor that delegates to the internal primary constructor with false/false.
The primary constructor is internal so the serializer in the same package can build an instance, matching the Swift required init(from:) role.
No Apple-only frameworks are used in this file, so nothing was replaced with TODO().
No comments were added; the full file is a single Kotlin file in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
Swift Character (grapheme cluster) indexing is translated to Kotlin UTF-16 Char indexing, so matches can differ for strings containing combining marks or non-BMP emoji.
The Swift `for shift in minShift ... maxShift` closed range can never be empty here because minShift <= 0 <= maxShift, so Kotlin's `minShift..maxShift` is safe.
Swift `func update(text newText: String)` becomes `fun update(newText: String)`; the external label is dropped as Kotlin has no argument labels.
`String.index(_:offsetBy:)` calls are replaced by direct Char indexing, with the same bounds guarantees (endOffset keeps offset + shift within oldText).
`abs`, `minOf` and `maxOf` come from kotlin.math and the Kotlin stdlib and preserve the original comparison semantics exactly.
Exactly one edit remains: there is no edit, as the source is pure logic with no Apple frameworks.
The `text` property stays private and is only mutated inside `update`; `position` remains a public var so callers keep the same API.
No coroutines, serialization or platform APIs are needed; the file is a self-contained class.
Subtitles is a plain class; the Swift `let length` computed in init becomes a Kotlin `val length` assigned once in an init block.
String length/indexing uses Kotlin UTF-16 offsets (`text.length`, `substring`) instead of Swift Character-based indices, so offsets differ for text containing surrogate pairs such as emoji.
`max(lastLinePosition, 0)` becomes `maxOf(lastLinePosition, 0)` since `max` is removed from Kotlin stdlib.
`.trim()` maps to Kotlin's built-in `String.trim()`, which trims whitespace like Moblin's String.trim() extension, so no extra extension is declared here.
The inner `offset` that shadows the outer one in updateSubtitles is kept with the same name for side-by-side readability (Kotlin emits a shadowing warning only).
`var lines: [String]` becomes `MutableList<String>` and array literals become `mutableListOf(...)` since `lines` is reassigned.
The `guard` statements become early returns, including the `offset < text.count` guard inside the firstLinePosition branch.
ObservableObject with @Published properties became private MutableStateFlow backing fields with public StateFlow exposure; setEnabled/setMicId replace direct assignment from outside.
The hand-written encode(to:)/init(from:) pair is realised by SettingsTalkbackSerializer, attached with @Serializable(with = ...), so the class itself keeps no serialization boilerplate.

Persisted JSON keys remain exactly "enabled" and "micId"; the private surrogate EncodedSettings carries @SerialName for both and gives them the Swift defaults (false / ""), so missing keys decode to the same values kotlinx.serialization fallback gave in Swift.
The nested CodingKeys enum is kept as an enum class with a rawValue property and a companion fromRawValue, matching the Swift coding keys byte for byte.
The empty Swift init() is the implicit no-arg Kotlin constructor; SettingsTalkback() is used by the deserializer to build the instance before applying decoded values.
EncodedSettings is an internal implementation detail of the port and has no counterpart in the Swift source.
any Encoder / any Decoder maps to kotlinx.serialization Encoder / Decoder.
CMVideoDimensions is not given a mapping in the port spec; it is translated to android.util.Size, which has the same width/height shape and value equality.
convertTo(dimension:) is assumed to be a top-level extension function on Size declared in this same package (com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.extension), so it needs no import here.
Swift Testing struct becomes a JUnit 4 class; @Test func becomes @Test fun with org.junit.Test.
#expect(a == b) becomes assertEquals(b, a) with kotlin.test, keeping the argument order of the Swift expectation.
There is no suite-level init in the Swift struct, so no @Before fun setUp() is generated.
All width/height literals are kept byte-identical to the Swift suite.
The Swift file-private constants become file-private Kotlin top-level `const val Double`s with identical camelCase names.

`AlertsEffectBackgroundLandmarkRectangle` keeps the Swift initializer shape: the constructor parameters have the same names and normalise by dividing by the reference image size inside the property initializers, so `AlertsEffectBackgroundLandmarkRectangle(topLeftX = ...)` call sites are identical and yield normalised values.
Because the Swift struct has custom init behaviour and methods, it is a plain `class` rather than a `data class` (no synthesised equality is provided by the Swift struct either).

Swift Testing struct suite translated to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions.

Failable enum initializers (init?(_:)) become companion functions fromString(value).

The Swift custom toString() on the unit enums is translated as override fun toString(): String.

Assumed the failable Swift initializers `HevcSeiPayloadTimeCode(reader:)`, `HevcNalUnit(data:offset:)` and `AvcNalUnit(data:offset:)` were ported as throwing constructors, so `try #require(...)` becomes a direct constructor call; if the port returns nullables instead, an explicit null check must be added here.

Byte literals above 0x7F keep their exact values and are written with `.toByte()` where Kotlin requires it.
CrcSwift.computeCrc8 has no Android equivalent, so it is reimplemented as the private top-level computeCrc8 (CRC-8, polynomial 0x07, initial 0x00), matching CrcSwift's default parameters.

#expect(a == b) became assertEquals(b, a), #expect(x == nil) became assertNull(x); assertion helpers keep their exact JSON text.

createAndGetDirectory and formatFilenameDateAndTime are called positionally to avoid depending on their Kotlin parameter names.
final class RecordingsStorage becomes a plain Kotlin class (final by default).

unsupported: URL(resolvingBookmarkData:bookmarkDataIsStale:) / startAccessingSecurityScopedResource security-scoped bookmarks

notes: encode() re-implements Apple's JSONEncoder output (keys sorted alphabetically, `"key" : value` separators, two-space pretty printing, '/' escaped as '\/') on top of kotlinx.serialization, so every expectation literal from the Swift suite is kept byte-identical.
Swift `try`/`throws` disappear: encode() returns String and never throws; the generic reified signature also serves the two non-request encode calls.

kotlinx.serialization prints Double(1.0) as '1.0' where Apple prints '1', so every literal whose expected JSON shows an integer (10, 30, 90, 250, 4200, 22, 17, 3...) was kept as an Int argument; decimals stay Double.

Foundation Measurement / UnitTemperature / UnitSpeed are replaced by the port's Measurement, UnitTemperature and UnitSpeed types in com.moblin.android.various, with celsius and metersPerSecond kept so the wire shape (unit.converter.coefficient/constant + symbol) is unchanged.
WeatherKit WeatherCondition.clear has no Android counterpart and is passed as its raw value "clear" (the string the Swift encoder produced).

Date(timeIntervalSince1970:) -> Instant.ofEpochSecond(...) and .now -> Instant.now(); note the expectation `"date" : 745043166` is Apple's 2001 reference-date encoding, which the port's serializer must keep to stay wire compatible.

Names for the sealed request cases were inferred from the Swift enum (RemoteControlRequest.SetGimbalTracking/SetGimbalMovement/AnimateGimbal/SaveGimbalPreset/SendMessage, motion RemoteControlRequest.GimbalMotion.Kapow), as were RunningMetrics and the nullable gForce accessors.

httpGet is assumed to be a suspend function returning Pair<ByteArray, NetworkResponse> that throws on transport errors, mirroring the iOS (Data, HTTPURLResponse) tuple plus thrown errors.
Emote is constructed with a String url (URL is only stored), so makeUrl(emote:) validates the string with java.net.URI and returns the string.
Dictionary merging with `{ $1 }` becomes MutableMap.putAll, which also keeps the newer value on duplicate keys; on failure nothing is merged because the fetch completes before putAll runs.
Swift's `throw "Not successful"` (String error) becomes throw Exception(...) because Kotlin can only throw Throwable.
The channel URL interpolates platform.rawValue, since the ported EmotesPlatform keeps the Swift raw value used by the BTTV API path.
JSONDecoder's tolerance for unknown keys is kept with Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }; optional CodingKeys map to nullable properties defaulting to null.
logger.info -> Log.i with the file-level tag "Bttv"; String(localized:) -> localized().
BttvEmote/BttvChannel remain private top-level @Serializable data classes and are decoded with explicit serializers.

@Published properties are translated as plain mutable properties instead of MutableStateFlow, because every one of these types is a persisted @Serializable settings payload that also implements Named (a String name); the observation layer lives outside this file.

Hand-written encode(to:)/init(from:) were replaced by @Serializable classes whose @SerialName keys match the Swift CodingKeys exactly, and every property keeps the same default value the Swift decoder used for a missing key.

java.util.UUID has no built-in kotlinx.serialization serializer, so id carries @Contextual; the SerializersModule passed to the settings Json instance must register a UUID serializer or id must be handled manually at runtime.
UInt16 ports (port, srtPort, srtlaPort, virtualDestinationPort) and Int32 latencies became Int, so makeUniqueVirtualDestinationPort() and srtlaSrtPort() return Int.
SettingsRistServerStream.connected is not part of the Swift CodingKeys, so it is marked @Transient to keep it out of the serialized payload.

SettingsRtspTransport keeps a rawValue property plus a fromRawValue() companion helper; its toString() overrides Any.toString() and yields the same strings as the Swift toString().
Identifiable has no counterpart declared in this port, so id stays a plain property and the classes only conform to Named.
@Published properties are translated to private MutableStateFlow fields exposed as read-only StateFlow; id stays a plain var because it is not @Published in Swift.

Codable's hand-written encode(to:)/init(from:) become a KSerializer implemented by each class's companion object (referenced with @Serializable(with = <Class>.Companion::class)); the CodingKeys enum is replaced by a private @Serializable surrogate whose property names match the Swift coding keys one-to-one.
java.util.UUID has no built-in kotlinx.serialization serializer, so ids are written to the wire as their canonical string form and parsed back with UUID.fromString.

The surrogate properties carry the same defaults as the Swift container.decode(_:_:_:) fallbacks, so missing keys decode to id = random UUID, name = "", enabled = false, printChat = false, faxMeowSound = true, printSnapshots = true.
Swift's empty init() {} maps to the implicit no-arg constructor, so both classes still have one.
SettingsCatPrinter.baseName lives in the companion object because Kotlin has no static stored properties.

String(localized:) -> localized(...); logger.info -> android.util.Log.i with tag "Ffz".

deinit { listener.cancel() } is dropped; Kotlin has no destructors, so the ServerSocket/coroutine scope is only released when the mock is garbage collected or the socket is closed via disconnect().
@MainActor / MainActor.assumeIsolated / Sendable conformances are dropped; the class runs on ordinary coroutines on Dispatchers.IO.
logger.info(...) is mapped to android.util.Log.i with tag "ObsWebSocketServerMock"; unit tests on the JVM need unitTests.returnDefaultValues or Robolectric for Log not to throw.
jsonString uses kotlinx.serialization and recursively sorts object keys to match Swift's .sortedKeys option.

AVAudioConverter has no Android counterpart; the conversion engine is android.media.MediaCodec and the pull based convert(to:error:withInputFrom:) becomes dequeueInputBuffer/queueInputBuffer plus dequeueOutputBuffer.
AudioStreamBasicDescription and AVAudioFormat are both represented by android.media.MediaFormat (KEY_SAMPLE_RATE, KEY_CHANNEL_COUNT, KEY_CHANNEL_MASK), which is what MediaCodec uses natively.
AVAudioCompressedBuffer maps to MediaSample from com.moblin.android.media; the CMSampleBuffer.withAudioBufferList wrapper is replaced by reading MediaSample.data.
The DispatchQueue lockQueue is a CoroutineDispatcher, and every lockQueue.async block becomes a launch on a CoroutineScope bound to that dispatcher.
The port's Atomic is assumed to expose a settable value, so bitrate.mutate { $0 = x } is written as bitrate.value = x.

setBitrate stays an extension function on the converter but only clamps and tracks the value, because Android audio encoders cannot change their bitrate after configure; the value takes effect on the next converter creation.

makeChannelLayout has no channel layout object on Android, so the discrete in order layout tag becomes a MediaFormat channel mask with the low channel bits set; both statics are consolidated into one companion object placed where makeAudioFormat appears in the Swift file.
As in the Swift source, setInputSourceFormat never assigns inSourceFormat, so that field is only cleared by stopRunningInternal; this behaviour is kept identical.
Swift enum with associated values became a sealed class with nested data classes (BundledName / CustomUrl / Image).
swift-collections Deque maps to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque; the deque is copied when handed to AlertsEffectGifImages to keep Swift value semantics.
SettingsWidgetAlertsAlertMediaType cases are assumed to be GIF_AND_SOUND and VIDEO (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE is the Kotlin convention).
URL is a String path, Bundle resource lookup becomes a File/asset lookup, and checkResourceIsReachable() becomes File.exists().
AVAsset/AVAssetReader audio extraction is re-implemented with MediaExtractor + MediaCodec, then downmixed to mono and linearly resampled to 48 kHz before createWav().
DispatchQueue.global()/main.async became a private file-level CoroutineScope; loadVideoSound() runs its work on Dispatchers.IO and delivers the callback on Dispatchers.Main.
getImage(presentationTimeStamp:) keeps the Swift basePresentationTimeStamp / drain-the-deque behaviour, including null when the deque empties.
decode-animated-gif (SDWebImage) and bundled Bundle.main lookups have no Android counterpart here, so they are TODO() placeholders.
unsupported: SDWebImage animated GIF frame decoding (ImageDecoder/AnimatedImageDrawable frame access not certain)
Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:) bundled alert media lookup

notes: FuzzyMatchingSwift has no Android equivalent, so its matcher is reimplemented in-file: a case-insensitive subsequence test combined with a Levenshtein similarity ratio, gated by the same threshold (0.34) and distance (1000) options.
The failable initializer init?(message:aliases:) becomes a companion `operator fun invoke(...)` returning `ChatBotCommand?`, so the call syntax `ChatBotCommand(message, aliases)` is preserved.
Swift Deque<String> becomes kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque<String>, using addLast / removeFirstOrNull / firstOrNull.

Kotlin has no CaseIterable; matchArgument and popFirstArgument take a reified type parameter bounded by Enum<T> and use enumValues<T>(). Both are `internal` so the inline bodies may reference each other.
Enum raw values are preserved byte-identically through an `override val rawValue` constructor parameter, including irregular ones: "wheelofluck", "4:3", "toggle-playback".
Swift enum case names are kept verbatim (lower camel case) as Kotlin enum constant names so both files read side by side.
Swift's split(separator: " ") drops empty subsequences; the Kotlin version filters empty strings before drop(1).
String.trim() / lowercased() map to Kotlin trim() / lowercase().
formatLog takes List<LogEntry> instead of Swift's Deque<LogEntry>: kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque would not accept the MutableList held by Model.log.
formatLog returns the written file's absolute path as String (URL -> String) and writes to context.cacheDir instead of FileManager temporaryDirectory, so Model must expose a context.
The temporary file name uses epoch millis ("Moblin-log-<millis>.txt") because Swift's Date() description contains characters that are awkward in Android file paths.

The extension functions assume Model exposes mutable collections/properties named log, fileLog, logId, logsStorage, logger, database, remoteControlLog and context; Kotlin extension functions cannot reach private members, so these must be internal or public in Model.kt.
logger.handler is assigned a lambda `{ message -> debugLog(message) }` because a bound callable reference to a private file-level extension function is not expressible as a plain (String) -> Unit.
DispatchQueue.main.async is dispatched on a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main).
formatDate(.now) became formatDate(Instant.now()) following the Date -> java.time.Instant mapping.
log.map { $0.message }.joined(separator: "\n") became joinToString(separator = "\n") { it.message }.
JUnit 4 with kotlin.test assertions replaces Swift Testing; the suite class name and all test method names are kept identical, and there is no suite init so no @Before is emitted.
makeRtmpUri(url:) and makeRtmpStreamKey(url:) are top-level functions from com.moblin.android.common.various and are called positionally.
RtmpConnection(name:queue:) loses the DispatchQueue argument; the Kotlin port creates the connection with the name only (queue becomes a dispatcher inside the class).
callCompletions is treated as a MutableMap<Int, (List<AsValue>) -> Unit>; the captured local var arguments is reassigned inside the lambda, which Kotlin allows.
Data slicing uses ByteArray.copyOfRange(from, to); the expected buffer equality is checked with contentEquals because ByteArray has no structural equals in Kotlin.
commandType is passed as RtmpChunkType.amf0Command - the Swift RtmpMessageType enum is represented by RtmpChunkType in this port, confirm the entry name.
The AMF result payload is built with AsObject(mutableMapOf("code" to AsValue.String(...))); confirm the AsObject/AsValue constructors in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.rtmp.amf.
makeConnectResultChunkData stays a private helper in the same file and returns a ByteArray produced by RtmpChunk.encode().
CoreImage has no Android counterpart: makeFilter now returns the raw 64x64x64 RGB key cube as a FloatArray and execute() is a TODO.
MetalPetal has no Android counterpart: executeMetalPetal() is a TODO and filterMetalPetal is kept as a null placeholder property.
MTIColor is replaced by the private data class MtiColor; SIMD2<Float> is replaced by FloatArray plus kotlin.math.hypot for distance/length.
CGFloat maps to Float and Double stays Double; the cube dimension 64 and the RGBA/alpha-offset layout are kept identical to the iOS version.
DispatchQueue.main and DispatchQueue.global() become the file-private CoroutineScopes mainScope and backgroundScope; asyncAfter(.now() + 0.25) becomes delay(250).
processorPipelineQueue is used as a CoroutineScope (launch); if the port declares it as a CoroutineDispatcher, change those calls to mainScope.launch(processorPipelineQueue).
@unchecked Sendable is dropped; the class is final and its mutable state is only touched from the same coroutine dispatchers as in Swift.
RgbColor.red/green/blue are assumed to be 0..255 components and hue() to return a Double in 0..1, matching the iOS types.
unsupported: CoreImage CIColorCubeWithColorSpace (makeFilter result and execute) - replaced by TODO()

notes: Swift Testing @Suite(.serialized) becomes a plain JUnit 4 class; JUnit already runs methods of one class serially, so no annotation is needed.
DispatchSemaphore -> CountDownLatch; FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory -> the java.io.tmpdir system property.
CMTime(value: 1, timescale: 30) is stored as a Long of microseconds (videoFrameDuration), and CMTime(seconds:) becomes a Long of microseconds.
AVAudioPCMBuffer / CVPixelBuffer sample creation is replaced by MediaSample instances built from raw PCM 16-bit little-endian bytes and a YUV420 frame buffer.
AVURLAsset and AVAssetReader track inspection are replaced by MediaExtractor plus MediaCodec decoding of the written mp4.
processorPipelineQueue.sync {} is assumed to be an ExecutorService submit/get on that top-level val from the same package.
Recorder.startRunning output settings are assumed to be android.media.MediaFormat values (AAC audio, AVC video) mirroring the AVFoundation dictionaries.
deinit file removal is translated into an AutoCloseable.close() on RecorderTester.

XMLCoder does not exist on Android: decoding uses javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory plus small org.w3c.dom helpers, encoding uses a hand-built string with an XmlNode.toXml(root) serializer (kept so Open and Auth keep their DynamicNodeEncoding attribute/element split).

URLSessionWebSocketTask is replaced by an OkHttp WebSocket; the callback-based listener pushes incoming text into a kotlinx Channel of unlimited capacity that receiveMessages() suspends on, and channel closure makes the receive throw so the reconnect loop still runs.
The @MainActor class keeps a private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) plus a Job; Task.isCancelled becomes coroutineContext.isActive, and sleep(seconds: 5) becomes delay(5000).
The hard-coded ws://192.168.50.72:5443/ws socket created in the Swift init is dropped, because the OkHttp socket is only created in setupConnection() from the real url property.
The Swift inout Int parameter of makeChatPostTextSegments is assumed to be intArrayOf(0) (a one-element IntArray) in the Kotlin port; adjust if that helper used a different convention.
model.appendChatMessage is called with named arguments matching the Swift labels, and the chat platform case is assumed to be ChatPlatform.openStreamingPlatform from com.moblin.android.various.model.
private top-level Swift structs become file-private (private) top-level Kotlin declarations in the same file, preserving declaration order.
The XML message is wrapped in <container> before parsing because XMLCoder matches the outer root's child element, exactly as in the Swift original.
The Swift tuple (displayName, segments, isAction) inside Delegate is replaced by a private DelegateMessage data class so messages is a MutableList<DelegateMessage>.
@MainActor is dropped; TwitchChat delegate callbacks are assumed to be invoked synchronously inside webSocketClientReceiveMessage, so the test can assert right after the call.
Swift multi-line string literals with trailing-backslash line continuations are rewritten as Kotlin string concatenation so the IRC wire text stays byte-identical.
try? X becomes runCatching { X }.getOrNull(); try #require(x) becomes a direct x.first() access with kotlin.test assertions.
#expect(a == nil) uses assertNull, #expect(!x) uses assertFalse, #expect(a == b) uses assertEquals(expected = b, actual = a).
URL.absoluteString comparisons become plain String comparisons: ChatMessageEmote.url and ChatPostUrl.still are treated as String URLs in the Android port.
twitchEmoteIds builds the path with java.net.URI and splits/filters empty components to match Swift String.split(omittingEmptySubsequences: true) semantics.
TwitchChatCommand cases are assumed to be PascalCase (PrivateMessage, UserNotice, ClearMsg, ClearChat, Ping) and userBadges/sourceChannelIcon are assumed String-based.

This is SwiftProtobuf generated code: the message model is translated to plain Kotlin classes, and the runtime encode/decode plumbing (SwiftProtobuf.Decoder / SwiftProtobuf.Visitor) has no counterpart in this port's stack, so those two methods keep their names but take Any parameters and are TODO().
UnknownStorage is represented as ByteArray, and equality uses contentEquals/contentHashCode.
Protobuf field presence is preserved exactly: nullable private backing field, computed property falling back to the proto default, a hasX property and a clearX() function.
The Swift enum init() (which selects .resultUnknown) cannot be an enum constructor in Kotlin, so it becomes the companion function defaultValue().
The bytecode-encoded _protobuf_nameMap is translated into an explicit Map of enum/proto name to field number, keeping the same property name.
static func == is expressed as equals()/hashCode() overrides since Kotlin has no static operator.
Sendable conformance has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped.
SwiftProtobuf.ProtobufAPIVersionCheck is kept as private marker interfaces plus a private object, since Kotlin has no nested typealias.
unsupported: SwiftProtobuf.Decoder
SwiftProtobuf.Visitor

notes: inout Int is modeled with kotlin.jvm.internal.Ref.IntRef; Emotes.createSegments is called positionally with that holder.
Swift's JSONSerialization-based decodeEvent is reimplemented with kotlinx.serialization Json.parseToJsonElement; the thrown String becomes IllegalStateException.
The shared Json instance sets ignoreUnknownKeys = true because Swift's JSONDecoder silently ignores unknown JSON keys.
URL(string:) validity checks are dropped: badge and emote URLs are plain Strings (ChatPostUrl(moving, still)).
logger.debug/info map to Log.d/Log.i with the tag "KickPusher".
@MainActor is dropped and the weak delegate is a plain nullable property; emotes callbacks are passed as function references.
getKickChannelInfo is invoked with a trailing lambda, assuming the ported API keeps its callback (non-suspend) signature.
All Decodable structs keep their snake_case JSON keys as Kotlin property names and are annotated @Serializable.
DispatchQueue is replaced by a CoroutineDispatcher constructor parameter plus an internal CoroutineScope; queue.async -> scope.launch and queue.asyncAfter -> scope.launch { delay(...) }.

AVFoundation types are mapped as follows: AVAudioFormat and CMFormatDescription -> android.media.MediaFormat, AVAudioCompressedBuffer -> ByteArray, CMTime -> Long microseconds, CMSampleBuffer -> MediaSample, so presentationTimeStamp.seconds becomes presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0.
MediaSample has no decode timestamp, so calcVideoCompositionTime returns 0 and the video sample path uses presentationTimeUs where the Swift code preferred decodeTimeStamp when it was valid.

Because AVAudioCompressedBuffer carries no AudioStreamBasicDescription, the audio codec is remembered in the new audioMime field set by audioEncoderOutputFormatInternal and checked with the literal "audio/opus".

The delegate overrides assume the port's AudioEncoderDelegate/VideoEncoderDelegate take (MediaFormat), (ByteArray, Long) and (VideoEncoder, MediaFormat)/(VideoEncoder, MediaSample, Long); adjust if the codec files chose other Android types.
RtmpConnection, RtmpChunk, RtmpChunkType, RtmpStreamInfo and RtmpStreamStats live in this same package, so they are used without imports; processorPipelineQueue is treated as a CoroutineScope.
SimpleTimer is built from the coroutine dispatcher and startSingleShot is called with a Double timeout in seconds (20.0), matching the Swift API.
info.bitrateStats.mutate { it.add(bytesTransferred = length) } is kept as-is, assuming RtmpStreamStats exposes the same mutate helper as the Swift version.
MessageKind entries are PascalCase (Null, One, Two, ...) because `null` is a reserved word in Kotlin; raw values are unchanged.

URLSessionWebSocketTask is replaced by an OkHttp WebSocket whose WebSocketListener pushes binary/text frames into an unlimited Channel, so the receive loop can simply await messages like Swift's `try await webSocket.receive()`.
The `webSocket` property is nullable because OkHttp starts connecting as soon as newWebSocket is called, unlike the dummy URLSessionWebSocketTask created in the Swift initializer.
Swift's String errors (`throw "Bad kind"`) become plain `Exception(message)` throws; the strict UTF-8 decoder keeps the 'Bad message not UTF-8' failure path intact.
`sleep(seconds: 5)` / `sleep(seconds: 60)` map to `sleep(5.0)` / `sleep(60.0)` imported from com.moblin.android.common.various.
Platform.Soop is assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.model (the type is not in the provided glossary); adjust the import if the Android port names it differently.

`emotes.createSegments(text:id:)` is called as `createSegments(message, id)` assuming the signature `(String, Int): List<ChatPostSegment>` (the Swift `inout` counter is only mutated and never read afterwards).

The "chat" subprotocol of `webSocketTask(with:protocols:)` is sent through the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header, and the POST body's content type is set via toRequestBody("application/x-www-form-urlencoded").

Every Codable class becomes an @Serializable kotlinx.serialization class; Swift optional properties get a Kotlin default of null so they are omitted from JSON exactly like the synthesized encodeIfPresent, while non-optional properties stay constructor parameters without defaults and are always encoded (and required when decoding).

The Swift encoder used .sortedKeys plus .withoutEscapingSlashes; toString() re-sorts every JsonObject key alphabetically (kotlinx.serialization has no sortedKeys option) and kotlinx does not escape '/' by default, so the output matches.
Swift throws String values as errors; in Kotlin those become Exception(message) with the identical message text, since String can no longer implement Throwable.
UInt32 bitrate and UInt16 port are wire-format values and map to UInt/UShort as required by the unsigned-type rule.
MoblinSettingsRemoteControlServerRelay conformed to ObservableObject but declares no @Published property here, so it translates to a plain serializable class without StateFlow.

MoblinSettingsRemoteControl keeps the Swift declaration order (assistant, streamer, password), which means the non-default 'password' parameter follows defaulted ones; callers must use named arguments.
fromString decodes with ignoreUnknownKeys = true because Swift's JSONDecoder silently skips keys that are not part of the model, while kotlinx.serialization throws by default.
fromString/toString both throw SerializationException on malformed JSON, replacing Swift's EncodingError/DecodingError.
libdatachannel's C API has no Android/JNI binding, so RtcTrack and PeerConnection keep their exact signatures but every native call site is TODO().
whipQueue becomes a single-thread CoroutineDispatcher; whipQueue.async maps to whipScope.launch and whipQueue.sync maps to runBlocking(whipQueue).
WhipStreamDelegate.whipStreamPerform now takes an OkHttp Request/Response with a (ByteArray?, Response?, Throwable?) completion instead of URLRequest/URLResponse/Error.
The encoder-delegate overrides were written against ByteArray, MediaFormat and MediaSample with Long microsecond timestamps; align them with the audio/video codec packages.
AVAudioCompressedBuffer is reduced to a ByteArray and its packet descriptions are dropped, matching Android's one-access-unit-per-buffer codec output.
DataChannelConnectionState and DataChannelGatheringState only exist in the Swift DataChannel module, so they are declared here with a fromValue(rawInt) companion.
Enum entries for SettingsStreamCodec (H264AVC/H265HEVC), SettingsStreamAudioCodec (OPUS/AAC) and the MpegTsVideoConfigAvc/Hevc create(format) factory are inferred.
logger.info/debug are replaced with Log.i/Log.d using the tag WhipStream.
unsupported: libdatachannel C API (rtcCreatePeerConnection, rtcAddTrackEx, rtcSendMessage, rtcSetLocalDescription, rtcSetRemoteDescription, rtcGetSelectedCandidatePair, rtcSetUserPointer and the open/closed/error/state/gathering callbacks) - no Android equivalent

notes: Swift `extension Model` becomes top-level extension functions on Model in the same package, keeping the original member names and order.

Kotlin has no retroactive protocol conformance: Model must declare `: BlackSharkCoolerDeviceDelegate` so that `delegate = this` compiles, and forward its two interface callbacks to these extension functions.
BlackSharkLib.CoolingState has no counterpart in the Android port, so blackSharkCoolerDeviceStatus receives phoneTemperature and heatsinkTemperature (Double) directly instead of the status object.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes mainScope.launch using a file-private `CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)`.
`device.bluetoothPeripheralId!` is translated to an early return on the nullable id (`?: return`) so it can be reused for the map key and the start call.
disableBlackSharkCoolerDevice keys the map by `device.id` exactly like the Swift source, not by bluetoothPeripheralId.
blackSharkCoolerDevices is expected to be a MutableMap<String, BlackSharkCoolerDevice> on Model, matching the Swift dictionary usage.

DockKit is Apple-only: every DockAccessory/DockAccessoryManager interaction (state observation, system tracking, orientation, animation, angular velocity, accessory events) is replaced by TODO("no Android counterpart for DockKit").
The Swift #if canImport(DockKit) / #else variants collapse into one Kotlin class whose public signatures match the stub branch; isConnected() still mirrors 'accessory != null'.
Spatial.Vector3D has no Android type, so a local data class Vector3D(x, y, z) is declared in this file; it is used only in gimbal signatures.
DockAccessory is kept untyped as Any? because its members do not exist in Kotlin; the private observer methods take Any for the same reason.
Fire-and-forget Task { } bodies become gimbalScope.launch { }, a private file-level CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) standing in for @MainActor + Task.
setOrientation/getCurrentOrientation are suspend functions; their '!tracking' guards and the nil result while tracking is enabled are preserved.

handleAccessoryEventCameraShutter/Flip/Zoom are fully translated against Model.database.gimbal, Model.handleControllerFunction and Model.setZoomX (Float conversions added because the Kotlin settings types are unknown).
Those camera event handlers stay unreachable until an Android gimbal backend feeds handleAccessoryEvent, which is itself a TODO.
unsupported: DockKit (DockAccessoryManager, DockAccessory, DockAccessory.StateChange, DockAccessory.AccessoryEvent, DockAccessory.Animation): no Android counterpart, replaced with TODO

notes: Swift's `throw "text"` is translated as `throw IllegalStateException("text")`; the `URL(string:)` guards were dropped because URLs are plain non-null Strings here.
`httpGet(request)` is assumed to be `suspend fun httpGet(request: Request): Pair<ByteArray, okhttp3.Response>`; `response.isSuccessful` keeps the same meaning as in Swift.
`Emotes.createSegments(text, id)` is assumed to return `Pair<List<ChatPostSegment>, Int>` (segments plus the next id), because Swift's `inout Int` has no Kotlin equivalent.
URLSession is replaced with OkHttp (`OkHttpClient`, `Request`, `Response`), including the POST upload with an `application/json` body.
JSON decoding uses a file-level `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }` instance and every Swift optional property got a `= null` default, so kotlinx.serialization tolerates missing keys.
`@MainActor` plus `Task` became a `MainScope()` coroutine stored as a `Job`; `Task.isCancelled` is `isActive` inside the launch block.
`sleep(seconds = 5.0)` and `sleep(milliSeconds = delay)` use the two overloads from `com.moblin.android.common.various`, and `delay` is a `Long`.
`ChatPostUrl(moving:, still:)` is constructed from String URLs, and the platform constant is `ChatPlatform.youTube` from `com.moblin.android.various` (not in the glossary).

Hand-written Codable encode(to:)/init(from:) with CodingKeys is translated to @Serializable classes with @SerialName per key; every property keeps the same default the Swift decoder used for a missing key.

@Published / ObservableObject is not mapped to MutableStateFlow here because these model objects are persisted with kotlinx.serialization (StateFlow fields cannot be serialized); the properties stay plain mutable vars and are observed by the Compose settings layer.
UInt32 bitrate is mapped to Int and Int32 to Int since no wire-format/byte-parsing code is involved.

kotlinx.serialization has no built-in serializer for java.util.UUID, so a top-level UuidSerializer (KSerializer<UUID>, encoded as a string exactly like Swift's Codable UUID) was added and applied to every id property.
DeepLinkCreatorStreamAudio.bitrateFloat is not encoded in Swift and was derived from bitrate in init(from:), so it is a @Transient computed property here.
DeepLinkCreatorStream.baseName is a static let, translated to a companion object property built with localized("My stream").
[T] arrays are MutableList because the settings objects are mutated; .init() becomes ClassName().
Identifiable has no Kotlin counterpart; the id property is kept and the class only declares the Named interface (from com.moblin.android.various.utils).
Swift Testing suite translated to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; the two async tests are wrapped in runBlocking.
NWListener/NWConnection from Network.framework are replaced with java.net.ServerSocket/java.net.Socket driven from coroutine IO loops.
Numeric assertions compare through toLong() on both sides because the ported RTMP fields (timestamp, length, streamId, sequence, size, protocolVersion) may be Int or UInt in the production types.
ByteArray comparisons use assertContentEquals because kotlin.test assertEquals compares arrays by reference.
AMF values are assumed to be the sealed Amf0Value type of this package with Object/String/Number/Bool/Null members; the command type is assumed to be RtmpCommandMessage.CommandType.
UInt32(x).bigEndian.data is replaced by the local private helper UInt.toBigEndianBytes() and Data(...).joined() by the local private joinBytes().
Enum entries keep the Swift lowerCamelCase case names (RtmpChunkType.zero, RtmpCommandName.releaseStream, RtmpMessageType.ack, ...).
Constructor and function arguments use plain integer literals so they adapt to Int, UInt or UShort parameters; suspend helpers are declared with UShort/UInt wire types.

Kotlin extensions cannot add interface conformance, so the GoProDeviceDelegate implementation of Model is emitted as a top-level extension function; Model must declare GoProDeviceDelegate in its own file and this function is the body used for it.
IndexSet is replaced by Set<Int>; the settings list is trimmed in descending index order so the remaining indices stay valid.
Swift switch expressions over RtmpUrlType and GoProDeviceState become Kotlin when expressions with uppercase enum entries (SERVER/CUSTOM, CONNECTING/STREAMING/WIFI_SETUP_FAILED/FAILED).
String(localized:) becomes the top-level localized() from package com.moblin.android.
The weak self/weak device captures of the Swift closures are dropped; the lambdas run on the calling coroutine scope and capture the extension receiver directly.
autoRestartStreamTimer is expected to expose startSingleShot(timeout: Double, onFire: () -> Unit) and stop(), matching the Swift timer wrapper.
NetworkInterfaceType, IpType and IpType.formatAddress are assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.model, hence no import is written for them.
Model members used but not declared here (goProDevices, database, getRtmpStream, makeToast, makeErrorToast) must already exist on Model.
iOS 18 availability guards are dropped; the Gimbal APIs are assumed always available in the Android port.
Apple's Spatial framework has no Android counterpart, so a local Vector3D data class is declared in this file; verify it matches the port's Gimbal.setMovement/setOrientation parameter types.
Task { } and DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter use a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main); the 0.3s deadline becomes delay(300) and defer becomes try/finally.
Deque.popFirst()/append() map to MutableList.removeFirstOrNull()/add() on Model.moveToGimbalPresetQueue.
String(localized:) maps to the top-level localized() function from package com.moblin.android.
error.localizedDescription maps to Throwable.message.
setQuickButton uses SettingsQuickButtonType.gimbalTracking, inferred from the Swift `.gimbalTracking` case; confirm that enum exists in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
makeErrorToast, setZoomX, setQuickButton and remoteControlStateChanged are Model members declared in other files and are called with the same argument labels as in Swift.
Model extension members became top-level extension functions on Model in the same package; cleanWizardUrl, createStreamFromWizardCustomUrl and createStreamFromWizardUrl remain file-private helpers.
WizardPlatform, WizardNetworkSetup and WizardCustomProtocol are Kotlin enum classes that keep the Swift case names and order.
URLComponents is replaced with java.net.URI and URLEncoder; validity of the parsed URL is expressed with runCatching(...).getOrNull().
Faithful to the Swift optional chaining: the SRT streamid is only set when the URL already contains a query string, so a URL without '?' is returned unchanged.
String(localized:) maps to localized() imported from com.moblin.android.
SettingsStream(name = ...) as well as the named arguments of makeErrorToast, setCurrentStream, sceneUpdated and the keychain helpers assume the ported signatures keep the Swift argument labels.
database.streams.add(stream) replaces Swift Array.append.
DefaultTcpPorts.mobcamStream from com.moblin.android.various.network is used to build the mobcam URL.
Swift `extension Model` members become top-level extension functions on Model in com.moblin.android.various.model; the private helpers stay `private` so they are only visible inside this file.

Swift `extension Model: DjiDeviceDelegate` cannot add interface conformance in Kotlin, so `djiDeviceStreamingState` is emitted as a top-level extension function; Model itself must declare `DjiDeviceDelegate` and the matching override in its own file for `djiDevice.delegate = this` to compile and for callbacks to arrive.
The `[weak self, weak device]` timer closures are plain Kotlin captures; on Android the ViewModel/Model lifetime is handled by the owning CoroutineScope, so no WeakReference is used.

`statusOther.ipStatuses` filtering compares `interfaceType`/`ipType` with their `.name` strings ("wifi"/"ipv4") because those enum types are not declared in this file's glossary and cannot be imported.
`device.autoRestartStreamTimer` is assumed to expose `startSingleShot(timeout) { }` and `stop()`; that timer type is declared with SettingsDjiDevice in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
Swift `IndexSet` offsets become `Set<Int>` and the removal is done over descending indices so that `removeAt` positions stay valid, mirroring SwiftUI's `remove(atOffsets:)`.
The `switch` over `rtmpUrlType` becomes an exhaustive `when`; the `switch` over `DjiDeviceState` keeps an `else -> {}` branch for the remaining states.
`String(localized:)` maps to the top-level `localized()` from com.moblin.android, which is imported explicitly.
Generated SwiftProtobuf file: every Swift enum became an enum class with rawValue plus a companion fromRawValue; the message structs became mutable Kotlin classes.
Swift's computed storage/`has...`/`clear...` triplets (protobuf field presence) are kept verbatim as backing nullable fields `_x`, a property with default, a `hasX` Boolean and a `clearX()` function.
`SwiftProtobuf._NameMap(bytecode:)` was decoded by hand into a plain `Map<Int, String>` (`protoMessageName` / `_protobuf_nameMap`) since the runtime no longer exists.

Swift's import Network is unnecessary on Android and is dropped; no Network.framework API from this file survives the port.

No Moblin-internal extension (utf8Data) is imported or redeclared, so this file has no dependency on other Moblin files.

The Swift file only wraps NetworkExtension's NEHotspotNetwork, which has no Android counterpart, so both function bodies are TODO stubs keeping the file's public API intact.
fetchCurrentWiFiSsid keeps the same callback shape: a top-level function taking (String?) -> Unit, so callers do not change.

The macCatalyst CoreWLAN dynamic-lookup helper is preserved as a private function of the same name with the same nullable String result.
On Android the equivalent read is WifiManager/ConnectivityManager plus location permission, but no such implementation is written here because this tier is a compile-compatibility stub.

No types are declared by this file, only top-level functions, so declared_types is empty.
