notes: Android's BluetoothAdapter/BluetoothLeScanner need a Context, so the constructor gains a leading context: Context parameter; the serviceIds parameter and its type (List<java.util.UUID>) keep their meaning.

CBPeripheral became android.bluetooth.BluetoothDevice, and discoveredPeripherals is exposed as a StateFlow<List<BluetoothDevice>> backed by a private MutableStateFlow (the @Published equivalent); CBPeripheral's RSSI is available in the ScanResult but was not stored because the Swift code discards it.

CBCentralManager maps to BluetoothLeScanner; the adapter is obtained from BluetoothManager and the delegate methods centralManagerDidUpdateState / didDiscover keep their names as private members (Swift's delegate extension cannot hold private state in Kotlin).
CBCentralManagerDelegate state updates arrive through a BroadcastReceiver on BluetoothAdapter.ACTION_STATE_CHANGED; the receiver is registered on API 33+ with Context.RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED.
CBCentralManager(queue: .main) has no direct counterpart: scanning starts on the calling thread and the class uses a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) for main-thread work.
The BLUETOOTH_SCAN (API 31+) / ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION permission is checked but never requested here; the Activity layer must request it before startScanningForDevices() is called.
CBUUID service filters map to ScanFilter.Builder().setServiceUuid(ParcelUuid(uuid)).
stopScanningForDevices() stops the scan, clears the scanner and unregisters the adapter-state receiver.
CoreMotion's CMMotionManager is replaced by android.hardware.SensorManager with TYPE_ACCELEROMETER; the constructor parameter motionManager is therefore named sensorManager.
motionManager.accelerometerUpdateInterval = 0.1 maps to a sampling period of 100_000 microseconds passed to registerListener.
startAccelerometerUpdates(to: .main) maps to registerListener with a Handler bound to Looper.getMainLooper(), so updates arrive on the main thread.
handleAccelerometerUpdate now takes x/y/z Doubles instead of CMAccelerometerData, since SensorEvent is only touched inside the private listener.
GForce is a @Serializable data class; its property names match the Swift coding keys exactly, so no @SerialName is needed.
getLatest() keeps the Swift optional return type GForce? even though the Swift implementation always returns a value.
start() now unregisters and resets the started flag when the device has no accelerometer, because getDefaultSensor can return null.
The SensorEventListener is a private anonymous listener so the public API of GForceManager stays identical to the Swift version.

CoreBluetooth maps to Android BLE: CBCentralManager -> BluetoothAdapter/BluetoothLeScanner, CBPeripheral -> android.bluetooth.BluetoothDevice, CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey -> ScanRecord.deviceName.
Peripheral identity uses BluetoothDevice.address instead of CBPeripheral.identifier (Swift UUID has no direct Android counterpart on BluetoothDevice), so the duplicate check compares addresses.

startScanningForDevices now takes a Context parameter because Android needs it for BluetoothManager and for registering the ACTION_STATE_CHANGED BroadcastReceiver; the Activity layer supplies it and handles runtime permissions.

centralManagerDidUpdateState is called from the adapter state BroadcastReceiver and takes BluetoothAdapter instead of CBCentralManager; the anonymous delegate methods were renamed to centralManagerDidUpdateState / centralManagerDidDiscover because Kotlin cannot overload the single Swift 'centralManager(_:...)' selector.
@MainActor / NSObject / ObservableObject are dropped; @Published discoveredDevices becomes a read-only StateFlow backed by a private MutableStateFlow, so callers can no longer assign to it directly.
goProControlServiceId is referenced as a top-level java.util.UUID in package com.moblin.android.integrations.gopro and is assumed to be declared in another file of that package.
String(localized: "Unknown") maps to the localized("Unknown") helper from package com.moblin.android.
stopScanningForDevices also unregisters the BluetoothAdapter state receiver that startScanningForDevices registered.
NWPathMonitor is replaced with ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback, so a Context parameter was added to the constructor because Android needs it.
NWInterface.InterfaceType has no Android counterpart and is replaced by a local InterfaceType enum keeping the same case names (cellular, wifi, wiredEthernet, other).
The DispatchQueue queue parameter is kept as a CoroutineDispatcher to preserve the public API shape but is not used by the Android connectivity callback.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin equivalent and was dropped.
Collections.Deque is replaced with kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque.
pathUpdateHandler is mapped to onCapabilitiesChanged; since only the default network is observed, .other is used when the network exposes none of the wifi/cellular/ethernet transports.
The `if self.cellular` guard is expressed as `this@NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector.cellular` inside the anonymous NetworkCallback.
The registration is never unregistered because the Swift file exposes no cancel path; the owner must call unregisterNetworkCallback if needed.

TeslaVehicleScanner is a ScanCallback subclass; the CBCentralManagerDelegate discovery callback became onScanResult(callbackType:result:) and keeps the same S[0-9a-f]{16}C whole-name filter and the same duplicate check.

startScanningForDevices gained a Context parameter because Android needs it to obtain BluetoothManager; the Activity must hold BLUETOOTH_SCAN (API 31+) or ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (below 31) before calling.
The @Published array became a private MutableStateFlow exposed as StateFlow<List<BluetoothDevice>>; duplicates are detected by BluetoothDevice.address instead of object identity.

centralManagerDidUpdateState(state: Int) mirrors centralManagerDidUpdateState(_:) and starts the LE scan when the state is BluetoothAdapter.STATE_ON; the Activity should call it from a BluetoothAdapter.ACTION_STATE_CHANGED receiver.
The Swift regex literal /S[0-9a-f]{16}C/ became Regex("S[0-9a-f]{16}C") used with Regex.matches, which anchors to the whole string like wholeMatch.
CBCentralManager maps to BluetoothLeScanner and CBPeripheral maps to BluetoothDevice; the scanner field keeps the name centralManager and is nulled after stopScan.
The advertised local name comes from ScanResult.scanRecord?.deviceName (the kCBAdvDataLocalName equivalent) and RSSI from ScanResult.rssi; LE scan callbacks are delivered on the main thread.
Bluetooth calls are annotated with @SuppressLint("MissingPermission") so lint passes; all runtime permission checks and requests are left to the Activity layer.
CBUUID strings '180D' and '2A37' are expanded to full 128-bit java.util.UUID using the Bluetooth base UUID.
CoreBluetooth CBCharacteristic is mapped to android.bluetooth.BluetoothGattCharacteristic.
The isBitSet extension is inlined as a bitwise check on the flags byte.
UInt8 and UInt16 in the wire parser are mapped to UByte and UShort respectively.
ByteReader from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util is used for parsing.
nonisolated(unsafe) is a Swift concurrency annotation and is omitted in Kotlin.
HeartRateMeasurement remains a private class at file scope.
handleMeasurement throws in Swift; in Kotlin exceptions propagate without an explicit throws clause.
CBUUID constants become java.util.UUID values built from the Bluetooth SIG base UUID; pass them to BluetoothGatt.getService/getCharacteristic.

ContinuousClock.Instant is replaced by monotonic Long nanoseconds from System.nanoTime(); WorkoutDeviceCrankCadence.update and the cadence state are assumed to use the same Long 'now' so the two files stay in sync.
The Swift Duration comparison of three seconds is inlined as 3_000_000_000L nanoseconds, and each averageSpeed.update call site keeps the Swift argument label as a Kotlin named argument.
The 32-bit wheel and 16-bit time counters stay UInt/UShort in the parsing struct, but all deltas are computed as Long so Kotlin's 32-bit Int cannot overflow on a counter wrap.

CyclingSpeedCadenceMeasurement keeps its throwing initializer as a secondary constructor that calls ByteReader; handleMeasurement simply lets the exception propagate because Kotlin has no checked-exception clause.
flags.isBitSet(index:) from the Swift UInt8 extension is re-implemented as a private file-level UByte extension function.
ByteReader is constructed positionally as ByteReader(value); align it with the Kotlin constructor parameter name if that file uses a different one.
CBCharacteristic is replaced by BluetoothGattCharacteristic; this class still performs no BLE I/O itself, it only stores the characteristic discovered by the caller.
CBUUID constants became java.util.UUID using the standard 16-bit Bluetooth base UUID expansion (1814 -> 00001814-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, 2A53 -> 00002a53-...).
CBCharacteristic is replaced by android.bluetooth.BluetoothGattCharacteristic; the setter/getter shape is unchanged.
ContinuousClock.Instant is replaced by SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos(); the elapsed seconds are the nanosecond difference divided by 1e9.
Swift's UInt8.isBitSet(index:) has no counterpart in the Kotlin ByteReader package, so a private file-level UByte.isBitSet extension is defined here.

ByteReader from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util is used for the little-endian reads (readUInt8/readUInt16Le/readUInt32Le); RscMeasurement and handleMeasurement keep Swift's throwing API via @Throws(IOException::class).
WorkoutDeviceRunningMetrics became a @Serializable data class whose nullable properties default to null, matching Swift's decodeIfPresent behaviour for missing keys.
RscMeasurement.totalDistanceMeters is declared as a var with a null default because Swift only assigns it when the total-distance flag bit is set.
Swift's nonisolated(unsafe) attribute on the two top-level constants has no Kotlin equivalent and was dropped.
A Context is now a constructor parameter because ConnectivityManager cannot be obtained without one; pass the application context.
NWPathMonitor is replaced by ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback with a main-Looper Handler, so callbacks arrive on the main thread like the Swift @MainActor code.
NWInterface.InterfaceType became the local InterfaceType enum, mapped from NetworkCapabilities transports (wifi/cellular/ethernet, otherwise other).

Swift's init only installed monitor.pathUpdateHandler; that handler is now the NetworkCallback overrides, so init just builds the callback object.
Swift URL is stored only, so pushUrl/stopUrl are plain String fields built from baseUrl and pushKey.
The failable init? becomes a regular primary constructor because there is no URL parsing failure path once URL is a String; call sites get a non-null RealtimeIrl.
CLLocation maps to android.location.Location: coordinate.latitude/longitude -> latitude/longitude, speed -> speed, altitude -> altitude, timestamp.timeIntervalSince1970 -> location.time / 1000.0.
The POST body is built as a plain JSON string like the Swift version; content type application/json is set via OkHttp MediaType.

Location permission requests are left to the Activity layer.
Network.framework NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; reads happen on a Dispatchers.IO coroutine and writes are fire-and-forget coroutines, matching .idempotent send semantics.
ContinuousClock.Instant is represented as monotonic Long nanoseconds from System.nanoTime(); isActive compares the delta against removeTimeoutNanos.
The Swift connection.batch / receiveMessage batch-of-100 pattern becomes a single blocking InputStream.read loop; connectionReceiveBatchSize is kept but unused.
A private ByteArray.setUInt32Be extension is added locally because the common package only guarantees createSrtlaPacket, srtControlTypeSize and the packet parsers.
logger.info/debug map to Log.i/Log.d with tag SrtlaServerClientConnection.

isSrtDataPacket, getSrtControlPacketType and getSrtSequenceNumber from the common package are used as ByteArray member extensions.

The three CBUUID literals were expanded to their full Bluetooth base UUID form (0000xxxx-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB) because java.util.UUID.fromString requires 128-bit strings; the characteristic values 1818/2A63/2A64 are unchanged.

ByteReader (com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util) is assumed to expose readUInt8(): UByte, readUInt16Le(): UShort, readUInt32Le(): UInt, readBytes(count): ByteArray and bytesAvailable: Int, matching the Swift parser and the wire-format unsigned rule.
Because the reader yields unsigned types, every isBitSet(index:) test was written as (flags.toInt() and (1 shl index)) != 0 to avoid relying on a helper that may not exist in the port.

The direction byte is masked/shifted as Int and converted with toUByte() before the enum lookup, matching the Swift UInt8 raw-value arithmetic.
handleMeasurement returns Pair<Int, Int?> instead of the Swift tuple (Int, Int?); handlePowerVector discards the parsed PowerVector like the original.
CBCharacteristic became android.bluetooth.BluetoothGattCharacteristic and Date.now became java.time.Instant.now(), which are the tier's platform counterparts.
WorkoutDeviceAverageCalculator and WorkoutDeviceCrankCadence are resolved from the same package com.moblin.android.integrations.workoutdevice, so no import is emitted for them.
CoreLocation maps to android.location: CLLocation -> Location, CLPlacemark -> Address, CLGeocoder -> android.location.Geocoder.
The class gains a Context constructor parameter because Geocoder needs one; every other member keeps its Swift name and signature.
@MainActor becomes a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main), and Task<Void, any Error> becomes kotlinx.coroutines.Job; the geocoding call is moved to Dispatchers.IO via withContext.

sleep(seconds:) is assumed to be the suspend function sleep(seconds: Int) from com.moblin.android.common.various; the delay variable stays an Int number of seconds.

Geocoder.getFromLocation is blocking, so it must not run on the main dispatcher.
Location.distanceTo returns Float while Swift returned CLLocationDistance (Double); the 1001/1000 literal fallback and threshold stay the same numbers.

CBCentralManagerDelegate is translated as a Kotlin extension function on Model; Android has no delegate protocol, so the caller must invoke it from a BroadcastReceiver on BluetoothAdapter.ACTION_STATE_CHANGED or after a permission result.

CBCentralManager.authorization == .allowedAlways becomes an explicit permission check: BLUETOOTH_CONNECT on API 31+ and BLUETOOTH below that, so a Context parameter was added to the extension function since Android permission queries need one.
The permission check itself lives in the top-level isBluetoothAllowed(context:) helper; no runtime permission request is performed here, that stays in the Activity layer as required.
ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission is used so no Google Play Services dependency is introduced.
CBCentralManager parameter maps to BluetoothAdapter? (obtained from BluetoothManager) and is unused, mirroring the ignored Swift parameter.
The assignment bluetoothAllowed = ... assumes Model exposes bluetoothAllowed as a public var backed by a MutableStateFlow in the port; if it is read-only there, expose a setter.

No MainActor equivalent is needed; the delegate callback runs on the caller's coroutine context.

WeatherKit has no Android counterpart, so WeatherService and Weather are kept as Any? placeholders and the weather fetch is TODO("no Android counterpart for WeatherKit"); the surrounding try/catch swallows the resulting error exactly like the Swift do/catch, so start() keeps looping.
@MainActor becomes a private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main); all state stays reachable from the main thread like the Swift actor isolation implied.
Task<Void, any Error>? becomes Job? and the Task { } block becomes mainScope.launch { }.
CLLocation is replaced by android.location.Location (platform tier); requesting the location permission is left to the Activity layer.
logger.debug(...) becomes Log.d("WeatherManager", ...) using the class name as the tag.
sleep(seconds:) is imported from com.moblin.android.common.various and called as a suspend function; the local delay counter is a Double so it matches the seconds parameter.

notes: NetServiceBrowser and NetService are replaced by android.net.nsd NsdManager discovery and resolve listeners; the class now implements NsdManager.DiscoveryListener and NsdManager.ResolveListener instead of the two NetService delegate protocols.
MoblinkScanner now takes a Context as its first constructor parameter, needed to obtain NsdManager via Context.NSD_SERVICE.
moblinkBonjourDomain is unused: android.net.nsd has no domain parameter, discovery always runs in the local domain.
resolve(withTimeout: 5.0) has no counterpart; NsdManager has no resolve timeout and failures arrive in onResolveFailed, which stays empty like the Swift file's missing didNotResolve.
service.addresses is reduced to NsdServiceInfo.host, so at most one websocket url is appended per resolved service.
Discovered services are matched by serviceName because NsdServiceInfo equality is not reliable across API levels.

@MainActor is dropped; the delegate is notified from a mainScope coroutine on Dispatchers.Main. The weak delegate reference cannot be expressed in Kotlin, so it is stored strongly in a nullable property.
NsdManager allows only one outstanding resolve per listener; onServiceFound resolves directly with this listener, so overlapping resolves can report onResolveFailed.

libsrt is reached through an `internal object SrtNative` declared in this file: it loads libsrt in its init block and exposes `external fun srt_setsockopt` with the same name and argument order as the C API. Keep a single SrtNative per package and extend it with the other srt_* calls as later files need them.

SRT_SOCKOPT and SRT_TRANSTYPE numbers come from the libsrt C header and are declared here as file-private const vals (srt.h 1.5 numbering); verify them against the libsrt fork bundled in the NDK build, SRTO_SRTLAPATCHES in particular.
snddropdelay keeps the raw option number 32 of the Swift source, exposed as the named constant SRTO_SNDDROPDELAY.

URL/URLComponents/removingPercentEncoding are replaced by android.net.Uri.queryParameterNames + getQueryParameter, which already percent-decodes values; getQueryItems therefore takes a String, not a URI.
Enum entry names stay lowercase exactly as in Swift so that rawValue (the query-string key, e.g. "srtlaPatches") is byte-identical.
MemoryLayout.size(ofValue:) is reproduced with fixed widths: Int -> 4 bytes, Int64 -> 8 bytes, written in native byte order (Android is little-endian).
The Swift enumeration branch sized its buffer from the String value (16 bytes) instead of the SRT_TRANSTYPE; the Kotlin version writes the intended 4-byte Int32 value.
logger.info(...) becomes Log.i with the class name as tag.
CoreBluetooth maps to android.bluetooth: CBCentralManager -> BluetoothAdapter (+ BluetoothLeScanner), CBPeripheral -> BluetoothDevice, CBCentralManagerDelegate callbacks -> ScanCallback.

@Published discoveredDevices becomes a MutableStateFlow exposed as a read-only StateFlow (private _discoveredDevices / public discoveredDevices); the singleton is the companion object property shared.

Android's ScanRecord strips the 2-byte company identifier, so the scan callback re-prepends it little-endian to keep manufacturerData byte-identical to the CoreBluetooth CBAdvertisementDataManufacturerDataKey payload expected by isDjiDevice/djiModelFromManufacturerData.
isDjiDevice and djiModelFromManufacturerData live in this same Kotlin package, so they are called positionally with the reconstructed ByteArray and need no import.
Data.hexString() has no counterpart in the glossary, so it is inlined with the stdlib: joinToString("") { "%02x".format(it) }.
The Swift delegate signature centralManager(_:didDiscover:advertisementData:rssi:) is collapsed into didDiscover(peripheral, manufacturerData); rssi was unused in the Swift body.
BluetoothAdapter state is checked in centralManagerDidUpdateState (kept name) instead of observing ACTION_STATE_CHANGED, and scanning uses ScanSettings.SCAN_MODE_LOW_LATENCY with no service filters.
BLUETOOTH_SCAN (API 31+) or BLUETOOTH + ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (API 26-30) must be requested and granted by the Activity layer before startScanningForDevices is called.
Model, StatusTopRight, LocationManager and the settings/database types are assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.model, so only RealtimeIrl and the Android/JDK types are imported.

CLLocation maps to android.location.Location: coordinate.latitude/longitude -> latitude/longitude, horizontalAccuracy -> accuracy, verticalAccuracy -> verticalAccuracyMeters, distance(from:) -> distanceTo() widened to Double.
The privacy-region loop assumes the region type exposes contains(latitude: Double, longitude: Double); the Swift version took a CLLocationCoordinate2D.
statusTopRight.location = location assumes StatusTopRight exposes a mutable location property (class with var), not an immutable data class.
ContinuousClock.Instant is replaced by monotonic Long nanoseconds from System.nanoTime(), so updateAverageSpeed takes now: Long and resetAverageSpeed stores System.nanoTime().
getLatestKnownLocation() returns Pair<Double, Double>? because Swift returns an optional tuple.
The Moblin LocationManager wrapper is used with the same call shape (status/stop/start/getLatestKnownLocation); the onUpdate callback is passed as a Kotlin lambda.
Location permission requests are left to the Activity layer; this file only starts/stops updates.

Kotlin cannot add protocol conformance from an extension, so Model's HttpProxyServerDelegate conformance is kept as the extension function httpProxyServerPortReady plus an anonymous adapter object assigned to HttpProxyServer.delegate.
NWEndpoint.hostPort is represented as java.net.InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", port) and NWEndpoint.Port as Int, so getHttpProxyServerEndpoint returns InetSocketAddress?.
Model must already declare httpProxyServer: HttpProxyServer?, httpProxyPort: Int? and database whose httpProxy exposes enabled, localNetwork and port.
setWebBrowserProxy() and setBrowserEffectsProxyServer() are resolved as Model members or extension functions in com.moblin.android.various.model.
DispatchQueue.main.async is replaced by a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) plus launch.
All functions are top-level extension functions on Model in this package, matching the Swift extension.
Network.framework NWConnection/NWListener are replaced by java.net.Socket / java.net.DatagramSocket running in coroutines on Dispatchers.IO; NWEndpoint host+port become String + Int.
The `weak var delegate` becomes a plain strong `var delegate` because Kotlin has no weak properties.
The original callback-driven receive chain is rebuilt as coroutine while-loops so a long stream does not grow the JVM stack.
Reading exactly N bytes is done with a loop over InputStream.read since Kotlin has no minimumIncompleteLength/maximumLength receive API.
stop() closes the sockets (to unblock the blocking reads) and then cancels the CoroutineScope.
ByteWriter (com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util) is assumed to expose writeUInt8(UByte), writeUInt16(UShort), writeBytes(ByteArray) and the `data` property.
logger.debug/info map to Log.d/Log.i with the tag "RtspTransport".
rtspTransportDisconnected() is never invoked because the Swift transport never calls it either.

WorkoutDevice extends BluetoothGattCallback; the CoreBluetooth delegate methods are kept as private functions (centralManagerDidUpdateState, connect, centralManagerDidConnect, centralManagerDidDisconnectPeripheral, peripheralDidDiscoverServices, ...) and are driven from onConnectionStateChange, onServicesDiscovered and onCharacteristicChanged.

CBCentralManager became BluetoothAdapter.getDefaultAdapter() (deprecated but context free); the java.util.UUID deviceId is handed to BluetoothAdapter.getRemoteDevice, which on Android expects a MAC address, so the caller must supply an address string.
BluetoothDevice.connectGatt needs a Context that this file does not have, so that argument is a TODO to be wired up by the Activity layer.

Android delivers a service together with its characteristics, so discoverCharacteristics has no counterpart: peripheralDidDiscoverServices forwards every matching service straight to peripheralDidDiscoverCharacteristicsFor.
Notifications are enabled with BluetoothGatt.setCharacteristicNotification; powering them with a CCCD descriptor write is left to the measurement classes.
Swift's private serial DispatchQueue is a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO) here, so calls into the device are no longer serialized on one queue.
Logging uses android.util.Log with tag "WorkoutDevice"; Data.hexString() is inlined as joinToString("%02x").
The Swift weak delegate is a plain nullable reference; clear it before releasing the device to avoid a leak.
unsupported: BluetoothDevice.connectGatt requires an Android Context which is not available in this file; it must be supplied by the Activity layer

notes: Network.framework NWConnection/NWListener are replaced with java.net.Socket/ServerSocket on Dispatchers.IO; the callback-driven receive loops became blocking read loops inside coroutines.
NWEndpoint is replaced by a host String plus a port Int, so HttpConnectRequestParser.Result carries destinationHost/destinationPort instead of an NWEndpoint.

The file-level serial DispatchQueue is a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO); Swift's serial execution guarantee is lost, so the shared `connections` list and `stopping` flag would need extra synchronization in production.
logger.info calls become android.util.Log.i with tag "HttpProxyServer".
HttpParser.getLine is assumed to return Pair<String, Int>? and HttpParser.data a ByteArray; both live in this same package so nothing is imported.
NWInterface/NWInterface.InterfaceType map to android.net.Network: NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector.getType() returns Network? and markBad takes it.
NWListener state updates are collapsed into handleStateUpdate(error: Exception?), where null means the ready state and a non-null value the failed state.
The body byte range is stored before connectToDestination runs (Swift sets it after the async connect) so the tunneling socket can flush it.
URLRequest is mapped to okhttp3.Request and Data to ByteArray throughout.
NWConnection/NWParameters are replaced by java.net.Socket on Dispatchers.IO, with TLS applied through SSLSocketFactory.
NWInterface interface cycling is preserved, but the default interface list must be resolved from ConnectivityManager and needs an Android Context (left as TODO).
@MainActor is represented by a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main + SupervisorJob()).
The createRequest tuple return is replaced by the private PlainRequest holder class.
Swift split(separator:) omits empty subsequences; the Kotlin splits filter out empty strings to match.
HttpResponseParser stays an open class hierarchy (HttpParser -> HttpResponseParser) as in the Swift source.
httpCallUrlSession uses OkHttp for the upload/body case and delegates the body-less case to the shared httpRequest() helper.

notes: Global `logger` becomes android.util.Log with tag "ObsWebSocket"; `logger.debugEnabled` maps to Log.isLoggable(TAG, Log.DEBUG).

The untyped JSON envelope (op/d/eventType/...) is parsed with org.json (the Android counterpart of JSONSerialization); typed payloads use kotlinx.serialization with ignoreUnknownKeys = true so unknown keys are skipped like Swift's JSONDecoder.
Swift's `throw "some string"` became IllegalStateException("..."), and `try?` became runCatching { ... }.getOrNull(); `try { } catch {}` became runCatching { }.onSuccess { }.
`weak let delegate` has no Kotlin equivalent: delegate is a strongly referenced constructor property, so the caller must drop the ObsWebSocket instance to break the cycle.

@MainActor is emulated with a private mainScope (CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)) used only inside the WebSocketClientDelegate callbacks; all public methods must be called from the main dispatcher as before.
The UInt64 event-subscription bitmask is kept as ULong (wire format) and serialized by kotlinx.serialization's built-in unsigned serializer.

Assumed WebSocketClient API (from com.moblin.android.various.network): constructor WebSocketClient(url: String, loopback: Boolean), var delegate: WebSocketClientDelegate?, start(), stop(), send(string) -- verify against the Kotlin port of WebSocketClient.kt.

`URL` is stored as String and `url.isLoopback()` (not present in the glossary) is replaced by a private isLoopback(String) helper using java.net.URI; request bodies are pre-encoded with Json.encodeToString at the call site because Kotlin cannot encode an `any Encodable`.

textToSpeechDispatchQueue becomes a single-thread CoroutineDispatcher backed by an Executor; every DispatchQueue.async block is a scope.launch on it, which keeps the serial FIFO ordering of the original queue.

AVSpeechSynthesizer is replaced by android.speech.tts.TextToSpeech; the synthesizer is typed as TextToSpeech and comes from createSpeechSynthesizer() so stop()/speak()/setVoice()/voices are available.

The AVSpeechSynthesizerDelegate extension becomes a UtteranceProgressListener (onDone/onError call sayFinished, onStop is a no-op) and the AVAudioPlayerDelegate extension becomes audioPlayerDidFinishPlaying(); audioPlayer.setDelegate(this) assumes this class satisfies the port's AudioPlayer delegate type.
Utterance rate/volume/pitch travel as TextToSpeech.Engine.KEY_PARAM_RATE/KEY_PARAM_VOLUME/KEY_PARAM_PITCH in a Bundle; AVSpeechUtterance.preUtteranceDelay is emulated with delay() before speaking.
AVSpeechSynthesisVoice(identifier:) and speechVoices() are replaced by lookups in TextToSpeech.voices matched on voice name and locale language.
ContinuousClock.Instant becomes System.nanoTime() nanoseconds, so the 30 second re-speak window is now + 30_000_000_000L and comparisons stay monotonic.
swift-collections Deque becomes kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque; delete(messageId:) and delete(userId:) erase to the same JVM signature, so the userId overload is annotated @JvmName("deleteByUserId").

SettingsVoiceType entries are assumed to be apple and ttsMonster, and KeepSpeakerAlivePlayer.shared.audioPlayed(), AudioPlayer(data), setDelegate, play and stop are assumed to exist as declared in com.moblin.android.various.
unsupported: NaturalLanguage NLLanguageRecognizer (dominant language detection and language hypotheses probability used by getVoice and isFilteredOutFilter)

notes: WiFiAware (Wi-Fi Aware listener/connection) and Network.framework's declarative NetworkListener/NetworkConnection have no counterpart in this port, so listen() keeps its signature and its body is TODO("no Android counterpart for WiFiAware").
actor WiFiAwareReceiver -> plain class with suspend members; the Swift 'static let shared' singleton becomes 'val shared' in the companion object.
private struct Sender -> file-private data class Sender; Swift Task<Void, Never> -> kotlinx.coroutines.Job, cancelled with task.cancel().
NetworkConnection<UDP> has no Kotlin type equivalent here, so 'connection' is typed Any; the Android realization of the UDP data path would be a java.net.DatagramSocket driven on Dispatchers.IO.
The 'connections' array is exposed as a file-private MutableList<Sender> of the class; actor isolation must be provided by a Mutex if the list is later mutated concurrently.
Swift 'async throws' becomes a suspend function; errors surface as thrown exceptions rather than a checked error type.
The '#if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)' compile guard and '@available(iOS 26, *)' annotations are dropped since they have no Kotlin meaning.
logger.info(...) lines disappear with the stubbed body; when the body is implemented use android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag.
unsupported: WiFiAware framework (Wi-Fi Aware listening, publishable/subscribable service pairing)
Network.framework declarative NetworkListener / NetworkConnection API

notes: NWListener/NWConnection (UDP) are replaced by one loopback DatagramSocket. The 'connection' is the remote InetSocketAddress of the first peer that sends a packet, and packets are sent back over that same socket so the local source port stays stable for the SRT peer.
onReady passes the port as Int because Android exposes ports as Int; UInt16 is only used for wire formats in this port.

srtlaClientQueue is assumed to be a CoroutineDispatcher/CoroutineContext, so the class builds CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + srtlaClientQueue). If it is declared as a CoroutineScope instead, replace this with srtlaClientQueue.launch { }.
NWListener.State is replaced by a private nested enum ListenerState(setup, ready, failed); setup is a no-op and every other failure maps to the same 'bad network state' error message as in Swift.
The receive loop drains incoming datagrams so the peer endpoint can be detected; the payload is discarded because the Swift file exposes no receive handler on its connection.
stop() closes the socket, which also unblocks the blocking DatagramSocket.receive; the scope itself is not cancelled so the listener can be started again.
DatagramSocket.send is blocking and therefore dispatched onto srtlaClientQueue from the non-suspend sendPacket().
All logging uses android.util.Log.i with tag LocalListener and the same message text as the Swift logger calls.
CoreBluetooth CBUUID becomes java.util.UUID; the 16-bit service id "FEA6" is expanded to its 128-bit base form 0000FEA6-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB so BluetoothGatt.getService(UUID) can match it.
Foundation Data becomes ByteArray: append/dropFirst/prefix/removeAll map to plus/copyOfRange/copyOf/ByteArray(0), and UInt8 counts are converted back with toByte().
All UInt8 wire constants are declared as UByte as required for byte-parsing code, so every byteArrayOf call site converts explicitly with toByte().
SwiftProtobuf's serializedData() is translated to com.google.protobuf.MessageLite.toByteArray() inside runCatching, matching the Swift try? fallback to an empty Data.

Generated protobuf member names (e.g. OpenGopro_EnumPairingFinishState.success, request.scanID, request.maxEntries, request.bypassEulaCheck, request.registerLiveStreamStatus, OpenGopro_EnumRegisterLiveStreamStatus.*) are assumed to mirror the SwiftProtobuf names in the Kotlin protobuf sources and should be checked against the generated code.
Swift nonisolated(unsafe) let top-level constants become plain top-level vals; there is no actor isolation to opt out of on Android.
The private SwiftProtobuf.Message extension became a private extension on MessageLite, so the eight message builders keep the exact same shape.
GoProBleMessageAccumulator is a plain class exactly as in Swift; no extra synchronisation was added, so callers keep their existing serialisation guarantees.
MoblinkStreamer gains a Context constructor parameter (first position) because the Bonjour advertisement now uses android.net.nsd.NsdManager; port/password/name keep the Swift names and order.
NWListener/NWConnection are replaced by java.net.ServerSocket plus a file-private WebSocketConnection that performs the RFC 6455 HTTP upgrade and frame coding on Dispatchers.IO.
NWConnection.start(queue:) has no equivalent and its call site was dropped: the Kotlin connection is usable as soon as the handshake helper returns it.
NWEndpoint is represented as host String + port Int, so MoblinkStreamerDelegate takes host/port instead of an endpoint object and Relay stores tunnelEndpointHost/tunnelEndpointPort.
moblinkBonjourDomain has no NsdManager counterpart, so only name/type/TXT attributes are registered.
@MainActor is modelled with CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main): all relay bookkeeping and delegate callbacks are dispatched there, so the mutable relay list needs no locks.
MainTimer, SimpleStringStorage(key:) and randomString() call sites assume the Kotlin ports kept the Swift labels; MainTimer intervals are passed as Double seconds per the TimeInterval mapping.

MoblinkRequest/MoblinkResponse/MoblinkMessageToRelay/MoblinkMessageToStreamer are matched with `is` checks and property names taken from the Swift case labels (id, result, data, apiVersion, authentication).
NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; connect, read and write run as coroutines on Dispatchers.IO and all blocking calls stay off the caller thread.
NWProtocolTLS.Options is mapped to javax.net.ssl.SSLContext? (null keeps plain TCP); an RTMPS caller passes an SSLContext whose socket factory creates the SSLSocket.

The DispatchQueue constructor argument became a CoroutineDispatcher named queue, still used for the delayed close and the too-much-buffered disconnect; short latency trickles stay on the caller side otherwise.
NWConnection.viabilityUpdateHandler has no Android counterpart, so viabilityDidChange is kept intact but must be driven by the caller (e.g. a ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback).
NWConnection.State has no Android counterpart; it is modelled by the private sealed class RtmpSocketConnectionState (Ready/Failed/Cancelled) declared in this file and fed from connect().
weak var delegate cannot be expressed in Kotlin; delegate is a plain nullable property and the owner must clear it when the socket is released.
RtmpChunk.split, RtmpMessage.length, RtmpHandshake.sigSize, RtmpHandshake.createC0C1Packet/createC2Packet and RtmpConnectionCode.eventData() are assumed from the sibling files of the same package.
logger.info is replaced by android.util.Log.i with the tag "RtmpSocket".
Location now takes a Context because CLLocationManager is replaced by LocationManager obtained from context.getSystemService.
CLLocationManagerDelegate maps to android.location.LocationListener, so the delegate callbacks are implemented inside the class body instead of a Swift extension.

The iOS authorization callback has no Android counterpart; locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization stays a public method the Activity layer calls after the permission dialog, and isDenied is derived from checkSelfPermission.
requestWhenInUseAuthorization is replaced by a permission check plus TODO(); ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION / ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION must be requested by the Activity layer.
CLBackgroundActivitySession has no Android counterpart, so BackgroundActivity.start and stop are TODO() (a foreground service would be needed).
desiredAccuracy maps onto android.location.Criteria plus getBestProvider; distanceFilter maps onto the minDistance metres argument with minTime 0 ms.
didFailWithError is mapped onto onProviderDisabled, the closest LocationListener callback; onProviderEnabled and onStatusChanged are required by the interface and are empty.
format(speed = ...) is called with a Double and isDenied is a StateFlow; the class must be used from the main thread.
unsupported: CLBackgroundActivitySession (BackgroundActivity.start/stop)
CLLocationManager.requestWhenInUseAuthorization (ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION must be requested by the Activity layer)

notes: Network.framework's NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; the NWConnection.stateUpdateHandler/NWConnection.State has no Android counterpart, so handleStateUpdate now takes a String state description and is invoked as 'ready'/'failed: ...' when the loopback socket connects or fails.
All blocking socket reads (receive loop) and writes happen inside a CoroutineScope built from srtlaServerQueue, which is assumed to be a CoroutineDispatcher (kotlinx.coroutines).

SRT wire values keep unsigned Kotlin types per the port rules: the NakPacket sequence numbers, timestamps and socket ids are UInt and the control-packet type/bit values are UShort (i.e. isSrtSnAcked(sn, ackSn) is called with UInt arguments).

The srtla.common helpers are called in their Swift free-function form (isSrtDataPacket(packet), getSrtControlPacketType(packet), getSrtSequenceNumber(packet), processSrtNak(packet) { }); if the sibling file declared them as ByteArray extension functions the calls only need a receiver/argument swap.
packet.getUInt32Be(8)/getUInt32Be(12) is assumed to exist as a ByteArray extension in com.moblin.android.media.srtla.common; it is not listed in the glossary but is used by the Swift file.
srtPort is an Int (port numbers are not wire-format data), and the loopback connection is created with InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1").
ContinuousClock.Instant is mapped to java.time.Instant, so duration comparisons use Duration.between(...) (millis for the 25 ms data flush, precise nanos for the 10 s client removal timeout).

NWConnection.batch/send(content:completion:) have no counterpart: the local SRT server socket is written through its OutputStream inside scope.launch, keeping Swift's 25 ms coalescing of data packets.
BlackSharkLib (the Swift cooler SDK) has no Android counterpart, so a local stub object with the same method names and TODO bodies was added; every call to it is therefore TODO.

CoreBluetooth: CBCentralManager/CBPeripheral/CBCharacteristic map to BluetoothAdapter/BluetoothDevice/BluetoothGatt + BluetoothGattCallback, so the class now takes an application Context in its constructor.

CBCentralManagerDelegate/CBPeripheralDelegate callbacks keep the Swift trailing labels as method names: centralManagerDidUpdateState, didConnect, didFailToConnect, didDisconnectPeripheral, didDiscoverServices, didDiscoverCharacteristicsFor, didUpdateValueFor.
The private dispatch queue becomes a CoroutineScope named blackSharkCoolerDeviceDispatchQueue; DispatchQueue.async becomes scope.launch.

ProcessInfo.ThermalState becomes com.moblin.android.various.storages.ThermalState, read from PowerManager.getCurrentThermalStatus() (API 29+, falls back to NOMINAL on API 26-28); its enum constants are assumed to be NOMINAL/FAIR/SERIOUS/CRITICAL.
ContinuousClock timing is replaced by System.currentTimeMillis() with the same 80 ms rate limit; writes are already throttled to 2 s by coolingStatsTimer.

BLE writes use the deprecated API-26 compatible path (characteristic.value/writeType + gatt.writeCharacteristic) since the value-carrying overload needs API 33; notifications are enabled by writing the 0x2902 CCCD descriptor.
CoolingState/UnknownMessage field names were inferred from their use in this file (phoneTemperature, heatsinkTemperature, fanRPM, powerLevel, rawData).
Apple-only tier: every HealthKit-touching body is TODO("no Android counterpart for HealthKit"); properties keep null defaults so callers still compile.
Workout stays a file-private singleton reached through Workout.shared; the HealthKit delegate protocols become plain member functions keeping the same names and parameters.

Kotlin has no argument labels, so add(heartRate:), add(cyclingPower:) and add(cyclingCadence:) become addHeartRate, addCyclingPower and addCyclingCadence; the private add(type:unit:value:) keeps its name.
WatchProtocolWorkoutType is declared here as a placeholder enum (WALKING, RUNNING, CYCLING) because the watch protocol file is not in the glossary; delete this declaration once that file is ported.
HKWorkoutSession, HKWorkoutBuilder, HKSampleType, HKQuantityType and HKUnit become Any, Date becomes java.time.Instant, ContinuousClock.Instant also becomes java.time.Instant.
Workout.isActive() and the private types() helper keep real implementations because they use no Apple API; the #available(iOS 26.0) guards are dropped.
The nonisolated delegate callbacks are not dispatched to the main queue any more: coroutine dispatch belongs in the ported watch/health layer, not in these TODO stubs.
Calls to logger, String(localized:), makeErrorToast and setIsWorkout vanish with the TODO bodies, so no logging or localization import is needed.
unsupported: HealthKit (HKHealthStore, HKWorkoutConfiguration, HKWorkoutSession, HKWorkoutSessionDelegate, HKLiveWorkoutBuilder, HKLiveWorkoutBuilderDelegate, HKLiveWorkoutDataSource, HKQuantitySample, HKUnit, HKSampleType, HKWorkoutSessionState)
WatchConnectivity (source of the WatchProtocolWorkoutType workout kinds)
ContinuousClock.Instant and HKWorkoutSession state transitions used for sample rate limiting

notes: NWInterface has no android.net.Network equivalent for type/name/index, so a file-local MoblinkRelayInterface wrapper (network, name, index, type) carries the values read from ConnectivityManager.

NWPathMonitor is replaced by ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback registered with a cellular/ethernet NetworkRequest; MoblinkRelay.applicationContext must be assigned by the Activity layer before start() so the ConnectivityManager can be obtained.

The UDP tunnel uses java.net.DatagramSocket receive loops on moblinkRelayQueue (Dispatchers.IO); NWListener/NWConnection state callbacks have no counterpart, so the listener-ready response and the waitingForCellular -> connected transitions are inlined in handleStartTunnel.
Android has no public API to bind a DatagramSocket to a specific android.net.Network, so the destination socket is created unbound; destinationInterface is only used to select and compare relays.
@MainActor is dropped; mainScope (Dispatchers.Main) and moblinkRelayQueue (Dispatchers.IO) replace the dispatch queues. The delegate is held strongly because Kotlin has no weak references.
UUID.add(data:) is replaced by java.util.UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes over relayId + interface name (then name becomes 'name-index').

Assumed Kotlin APIs from the port: WebSocketClient(url[, cellular]), send(string), delegate; WebSocketClientDelegate.webSocketClientConnected/Disconnected/ReceiveMessage; MainTimer.startSingleShot(timeout, handler); SimpleStringStorage.get()/set(); Moblink* sealed subclasses and remoteControlHashPassword(challenge, salt, password).
MoblinkRelayState and RelayState keep their Swift raw values through a rawValue property plus a fromRawValue companion helper.

CoreBluetooth delegate methods become ordinary class methods invoked from a private BluetoothGattCallback; the Swift overloads centralManager(_:didConnect:), centralManager(_:didFailToConnect:error:), centralManager(_:didDisconnectPeripheral:error:) and peripheral(_:didDiscover...) get distinct Kotlin names (centralManagerDidConnect, centralManagerDidFailToConnect, ...).
DjiDevice now takes an android.content.Context constructor argument because BluetoothDevice.connectGatt() requires one; nothing else about the public API changes.

CBCentralManager.retrievePeripherals(withIdentifiers:) has no Android equivalent, so central.getRemoteDevice(deviceId.toString()) wrapped in runCatching is used (Android identifies BLE peripherals by MAC address, not by UUID).

Android requires an explicit CCCD write to enable notifications, so a private cccdId UUID and a descriptor write were added in peripheralDidDiscoverCharacteristicsFor, and peripheralDidUpdateNotificationStateFor is driven from BluetoothGattCallback.onDescriptorWrite.

DjiMessage(data:) is assumed to exist as a Kotlin constructor; the corrupt-packet parse uses runCatching { DjiMessage(value) }.getOrNull() and the iOS hexString() helper is inlined as joinToString with "%02x".
Transaction ids and targets are UShort, message types are UInt and bitrate is UInt, matching the DJI wire format.
MainTimer is assumed to expose startSingleShot(timeout: Double) and stop() in Kotlin, and the timeout is passed as Double seconds (60.0 / 10.0).

model.hasNewProtocol(), videoCodec.toDjiCodec()/toDjiEnhancedRtmp() and DjiStartStreamingMessagePayload2.osmoPocket4Header/osmoAction6Header are assumed to keep their Swift names; enum cases keep the Swift lowerCamelCase names (DjiDeviceState.idle, SettingsDjiDeviceModel.osmoAction2, ...).
Actor -> class with a companion object holding `shared`; the connection table is a ConcurrentHashMap so it is safe from the launched tasks.
Task<Void, Never> -> Job from scope.launch; sleep(seconds: 5) -> delay(5_000); the sender/receiver closure bodies map onto coroutines on Dispatchers.IO.

NWConnection over UDP -> java.net.DatagramSocket; send/receive build and fill DatagramPacket instances, and the peer address comes from remoteSocketAddress, so the socket handed over must already be connected to the peer.

WiFiAware (NetworkBrowser, NetworkConnection, WAPairedDevice) is only reachable through the private suspend helper browseWiFiAware, which is a TODO; on Android this is android.net.wifi.aware (attach/publish/subscribe + WifiAwareNetworkSpecifier) or NetLink ServiceDiscovery.
WAPairedDevice.ID -> String device id used as the map key.
The Swift `try?` around browser.run disappears: browseWiFiAware throws NotImplementedError until it is implemented, so the cleanup and 'Stop' logging after it do not run yet.
DatagramSocket.receive is blocking, so cancelling the receiver task only ends the loop once a packet arrives or the socket is closed.
Receiver keeps the same three stored properties in the same order, with senderTask/receiverTask as Job.
unsupported: WiFiAware NetworkBrowser / NetworkConnection over UDP (Network.framework on Wi-Fi Aware)

notes: DispatchQueue ristQueue became a single-thread coroutine dispatcher (ristDispatcher) plus a CoroutineScope (ristScope); ristQueue.sync { } blocks map to runBlocking(ristDispatcher) { }, ristQueue.async/named queues map to scope.launch.

The Rist C library has no ready JNI binding, so its types (RistPeer, RistSenderContext, RistSenderStats, RistStats, RistSenderContextDelegate) are declared in this file following the libsrt rule: the wrapper keeps the Swift method names and calls a private RistNative object with external fun declarations and System.loadLibrary("rist").
NWEndpoint is replaced by RistEndpoint(host, port); NWInterface.InterfaceType is replaced by an android.net.NetworkCapabilities transport constant (Int?).

NWPathMonitor is replaced by ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback; because a Context is required, the file exposes a top level var ristApplicationContext that the Activity layer must set before starting a bonding stream.
Swift weak references (weak let stream, weak let ristDelegate) became plain strong references; Java GC handles the resulting cycles.
deinit has no Kotlin counterpart and became a close() method that stops the connecting timer; stopInternal also calls close() on removed peers.

MpegTsWriterDelegate and RistSenderContextDelegate overrides keep the Swift parameter names; the exact Kotlin delegate signatures come from the ported Moblin interfaces in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg and are assumed to match.
SimpleTimer(ristScope), Atomic<Long>(0L), processorPipelineQueue.launch { } and BondingConnection(name:, usage:, rtt:) use the signatures of the ported types listed in the glossary.

NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket: connect, receive and send run in coroutines on the file-private connectionScope (Dispatchers.IO + SupervisorJob); srtlaClientQueue is still what the two SimpleTimer instances are built with.

NWInterface.InterfaceType has no Android counterpart, so `type` is an Int? holding android.net.NetworkCapabilities.TRANSPORT_* values (null means relay/any), and NWParameters.requiredInterface is applied by creating the socket through Network.socketFactory.
Because android.net.Network exposes no interface name, the typeString lookup uses interface?.toString() as the key into SrtlaNetworkInterfaces.names.
NWConnection.State has no Android counterpart: a private top-level ConnectionState enum (ready/failed) stands in for the handleStateUpdate(to:) parameter.
ContinuousClock instants become System.nanoTime(); getKeepAliveTime() and rtt stay millisecond based like the Swift code.

The Data helpers used by this file (getUInt32Be, setUInt32Be, getInt64Be, setInt64Be, randomData) are not part of the glossary, so they are declared as private top-level ByteArray extensions here, implemented with ByteBuffer and SecureRandom.
logger.* maps to android.util.Log with tag RemoteConnection; the weak delegate becomes a strong reference, and deinit is translated as an override of finalize().

sizeFormatter (com.moblin.android.common.various) is assumed to expose format(bytes: Long): String for ByteCountFormatter.string(fromByteCount:), and outgoing packets are written under synchronized(socket) so they cannot interleave.

srtlaClientQueue is a single-thread CoroutineDispatcher: DispatchQueue.async becomes srtlaClientScope.launch and DispatchQueue.sync becomes runBlocking(srtlaClientQueue) (never call those two sync-based getters from the srtla dispatcher itself).

NWPathMonitor/NWPath are replaced by ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback plus a Network->transport map; no Context is available in this layer, so the ConnectivityManager must be published through the new top-level var srtlaConnectivityManager by the Activity (TODO until then).

NWEndpoint parameters are flattened into host: String + port: Int (addMoblink/removeMoblink/startRemote) and NWInterface becomes android.net.Network with its NetworkCapabilities.TRANSPORT_* constant as the interface type.
UInt16 ports became Int, UInt32 sequence numbers became UInt, and ContinuousClock/Duration became System.nanoTime() nanoseconds compared against 15_000_000L.
deinit has no Kotlin counterpart, so the 'srtla deinit' debug log is dropped.
weak let delegate becomes a plain nullable reference (private val delegate: SrtlaDelegate?) since Kotlin has no weak properties.

notes: Network.framework NWListener/NWConnection are replaced by java.net.ServerSocket/Socket; the accept loop and each connection read loop run as coroutines on Dispatchers.IO.

HttpServer.queue is modelled as a CoroutineDispatcher and the class exposes an internal scope so HttpServerConnection can share it; SimpleTimer is assumed to be constructible as SimpleTimer(queue: CoroutineDispatcher).
NWEndpoint.Port becomes Int (default 80); the NWListener.State failure branch became handleStateUpdate(failed: Boolean) driving the same 1 second retry through retryTimer.
sendFileAndClose takes a java.io.File and streams it in 512 KiB blocking chunks (iterative loop) instead of the recursive NWConnection completion chain.

HttpServerConnection is internal instead of fileprivate because it appears in HttpServerResponse's internal constructor; HttpServerResponse.connection is a plain nullable reference (Kotlin has no weak properties).
HttpParser, declared in the same package, is assumed to be an open class exposing data: ByteArray, append(data: ByteArray) and getLine(data: ByteArray, offset: Int): Pair<String, Int>?.
Data.advanced(by:)/prefix become ByteArray.copyOfRange/copyOf; utf8Data becomes String.toByteArray().
logger.debug/info become Log.d/Log.i with a file level TAG constant because Kotlin has no per-class logger.
unsupported: NWListener.Service (Bonjour/mDNS advertisement) replaced by TODO("register mDNS service with NsdManager")

notes: @MainActor protocol becomes a plain interface; SDK callbacks (webSocket*) are hopped onto Dispatchers.Main through mainScope so delegate calls stay on the main thread.
Swift 'private weak let delegate' has no Kotlin equivalent; it is a strong nullable property. Callers must drop their delegate reference explicitly to avoid leaking.
URL -> String (stored only). URL.isLoopback() is not in the glossary, so it is re-implemented here as a private String extension using java.net.URI.

Sealed cases of RemoteControlMessageToStreamer / RemoteControlRequest / RemoteControlResponse / RemoteControlEvent / RemoteControlMessageToAssistant are assumed to be named after the Swift cases with a capital first letter (Hello, Request, GetStatus, Response, ...) and their properties after the Swift labels.
RemoteControlResult is treated as an enum class whose entries keep the Swift case names (ok, wrongPassword, error) because the raw values are persisted.
Data -> ByteArray, base64EncodedString() -> android.util.Base64.encodeToString(..., Base64.NO_WRAP); Data.utf8Data -> String.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8).
String(localized:) -> localized() imported from com.moblin.android; logger -> android.util.Log with the file-level TAG.
UUID().uuidString -> UUID.randomUUID().toString() (lowercase, the wire value is still a valid UUID).
The Info.plist lookup for MoblinWebsiteApiUrl is replaced by BuildConfig.MOBLIN_WEBSITE_API_URL; that buildConfigField has to be added to the app module.
DeviceCheck App Attest has no Android counterpart, so attestedKey(), sendLive() and generateAssertion() are TODO(); fetchChallenge() and postLive() keep the whole HTTP flow.
URLSession is replaced by a shared OkHttpClient with 30 s timeouts, and every request runs on Dispatchers.IO.
CryptoKit SHA256 becomes MessageDigest("SHA-256") and Data.base64EncodedString() becomes java.util.Base64 (API 26+).
The Codable structs become @Serializable classes with identical field names; Data becomes ByteArray, which kotlinx.serialization writes as a JSON number array instead of base64.
MoblinWebsiteError is a sealed class extending Exception with the KeyRejected and BadResponse subclasses.

The Twitch/YouTube/Kick callbacks are bridged with suspendCancellableCoroutine; createTwitchApi, getYouTubeApi, createKickApi and the listChannels result type (YouTubeApiResult.Success) must match their own ports.
defer { onCompleted?() } becomes try/finally inside a mainScope.launch block, so the @MainActor completion still runs on the main thread.
unsupported: DeviceCheck DCAppAttestService.generateKey/attestKey/isSupported (App Attest) - attestedKey() and sendLive() bodies are TODO()
DeviceCheck DCAppAttestService.generateAssertion - generateAssertion() body is TODO()

notes: NWListener/NWConnection are replaced by java.net.ServerSocket plus a private RemoteControlWebSocket class implementing the RFC 6455 upgrade handshake and framing, because OkHttp has no server-side WebSocket; receivePacket/handleMessage are subsumed by RemoteControlWebSocket.readLoop().
@MainActor state is confined to mainScope (Dispatchers.Main), all socket IO runs on ioScope (Dispatchers.IO), and every NWConnection callback is re-dispatched onto mainScope.
port is Int instead of UInt16 so it can be passed to ServerSocket.bind().
`private weak let delegate` is preserved with java.lang.ref.WeakReference behind a read-only `delegate` accessor, so all call sites keep the original shape.

Sealed-class case constructors are assumed to be nested and named after the Swift cases (RemoteControlRequest.GetStatus, RemoteControlMessageToStreamer.Hello, RemoteControlMessageToAssistant.Identify, RemoteControlResponse.Whip, RemoteControlResult.Ok, ...); adjust if the real port uses factory functions.

HTTPURLResponse is replaced by a hand-built okhttp3.Response in whipPerform(); URL-typed values (userBadges, sourceChannelIcon) are kept as String, and digitalClockFormatter is assumed to be a java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter fed with ZonedDateTime.now().

Deque<RemoteControlChatMessage> became java.util.ArrayDeque; RemoteControlChatMessage.platform uses RemoteControlChatMessage.Platform.Twitch and highlight uses the ChatHighlight.toRemoteControl() extension.

MainTimer from com.moblin.android.various keeps the original startSingleShot/startPeriodic/stop calls; the TwitchEventSubDelegate and TwitchChatDelegate conformances are moved into the class body since Kotlin has no extensions implementing interfaces.
RemoteControlWebDelegate becomes a Kotlin interface; the Swift `weak` delegate is stored as a plain nullable property because Kotlin has no weak references for interfaces.

Network.framework NWListener/NWConnection is replaced with java.net.ServerSocket plus a hand-rolled RFC6455 WebSocket handshake and frame codec running on Dispatchers.IO; callbacks are dispatched back on a Dispatchers.Main scope.
NWListener.State update handling is reduced to a private `handleWebsocketStateUpdate(failed: Boolean)` helper that drives the same 1s retry timer.
UInt16 ports become Int (ServerSocket takes Int); string interpolation on the port value is preserved in config.mjs.
URL return of `remoteControlWebGetRecordingUrl` maps to java.net.URI; `[[String: String]]` recordings map to List<Map<String, String>>.
JSONSerialization is replaced with org.json.JSONArray and logger.info with android.util.Log.i using the class name as tag.
Sealed-class case names are assumed as RemoteControlRequest.*, RemoteControlResponse.*, RemoteControlMessageToAssistant.* and RemoteControlEvent.* (PascalCase, matching the Swift case labels).
@MainActor isolation is not reproduced; blocking socket work runs on Dispatchers.IO and UI-visible callbacks run on Dispatchers.Main.
unsupported: NetService Bonjour advertisement (`_http._tcp` passed to HttpServer) has no Android counterpart and is passed as TODO()

notes: Model is declared in the same package, so this file holds top-level extension functions on Model; the Swift file-private `thumbStickDeadZone` became a private top-level `const val`.

GameController has no Android counterpart: GCController is replaced by android.view.InputDevice and the per-button `pressedChangedHandler` / `valueChangedHandler` wiring is gone because the Activity delivers KeyEvent/MotionEvent instead.
`handleGameControllerButton` and `handleGameControllerThumbStick` were private in Swift and are left public on purpose so the Activity layer can forward key and motion events into them.
`button.sfSymbolsName` is replaced by an explicit `buttonId: String` parameter; the Activity is expected to map KeyEvent key codes to the same ids stored in SettingsGameControllerButton.name.
`String(localized:)` became the top-level `localized()` function imported from com.moblin.android.
`Gimbal.shared?.animate(motion:)` keeps the `shared` accessor shape; the iOS 18 availability check is dropped since it does not exist on Android.
The `[weak self]` capture in the gimbal preset long-press timer is dropped; Kotlin lambdas capture strongly, so the timer must be stopped/removed to avoid retaining the Model.
SettingsQuickButtonType is not in the glossary and is assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.settings; fix the import if the port placed it elsewhere.
CoreBluetooth is replaced by BluetoothAdapter/BluetoothLeScanner/BluetoothGatt; a Context constructor parameter was added because BluetoothManager needs it.

Swift resolves the peripheral with CBCentralManager.retrievePeripherals(withIdentifiers:); Android cannot map a CoreBluetooth UUID to a MAC address, so a BLE scan is started and the first result is connected.
BluetoothGatt callbacks arrive on a binder thread, so every callback override posts to mainScope to keep the @MainActor semantics of the Swift class.
Enabling notifications needs an explicit CCCD write, so the client characteristic configuration descriptor id 00002902-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb was added.

The ported protobuf types are assumed to keep the SwiftProtobuf accessor names (result, hasTimeoutSeconds, timeoutSeconds, entries, scanID, liveStreamLensSupportedArray) and to be parsed with parseFrom().
Characteristic writes use BluetoothGattCharacteristic.setValue + BluetoothGatt.writeCharacteristic (pre-API-33 API) so the code works down to API 26.
MainTimer, the goPro* constants and the goPro*Message helpers are taken from com.moblin.android.integrations.gopro / com.moblin.android.various as given in the glossary.
Runtime permissions (BLUETOOTH_SCAN/CONNECT or ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION) are left to the activity layer; the class is annotated with @SuppressLint("MissingPermission").
@MainActor is dropped: these Model extensions run on the main dispatcher like the rest of Model.
The three WatchConnectivity entry points keep their names but their bodies are TODO(...) because the WatchProtocol* payload types have no Android counterpart; their parameters are typed Any.
The scoreboard configs stay file-private top-level vals; configs is declared after the individual configs so top-level initialisation order matches Swift.
Swift switch expressions on scoreboard.sport become when(...) with an else branch, and if/guard let becomes a null check, ?.let or an early return.
clamped(to:) maps to coerceIn, Array.popLast()/removeLast() map to MutableList.removeLastOrNull()/removeLast(), count is read through List.size.

modular.layout and modular.clock.direction are compared against SettingsWidgetScoreboardLayout and SettingsWidgetGenericScoreboardClockDirection taken from the glossary; verify these are the enums used by SettingsWidgetModularScoreboard.
scoreChanges elements are translated as SettingsWidgetScoreboardScoreIncrement.home/.away, and padel/generic score entries as SettingsWidgetScoreboardScore().

modular.home.textColor.toHex() is kept as a member call on the color type of com.moblin.android.common.various, and modular.clock.format() is imported as the top-level extension format() from that package.
unsupported: WatchConnectivity (WatchProtocolPadelScoreboardAction, WatchProtocolPadelScoreboardActionPlayers)

notes: CoreBluetooth maps to BluetoothAdapter/BluetoothGatt/BluetoothGattCallback; the CBCentralManagerDelegate and CBPeripheralDelegate extensions are merged into the Android callbacks onConnectionStateChange, onServicesDiscovered, onCharacteristicChanged and onCharacteristicWrite.

peripheralId is a CoreBluetooth UUID; Android resolves a peripheral from its Bluetooth MAC address, so the identifier stored by the app must be the MAC address passed to BluetoothAdapter.getRemoteDevice.

CryptoKit P-256, SHA-1/SHA-256 and AES-GCM are replaced by JCA: KeyAgreement ECDH, MessageDigest and Cipher AES/GCM/NoPadding, with the tag and ciphertext split out of the sealed output by hand because the JCA returns them concatenated.
CryptoKit exposes .publicKey on a private key; JCA does not, so the raw public point is read from the publicKey BIT STRING of the PKCS#8 DER (privateKeyFromPem, ecPublicKeyBytesFromPem, derContent).

The protobuf types (UniversalMessage_*, Signatures_*, VCSEC_*, CarServer_*) are not in the glossary; they are assumed to be generated into this package with mutable ByteArray/Int properties and enum number values, matching the flattened names the Swift code already uses.
responseHandlers is keyed by the hex string of the routing address because ByteArray has no value equality.
BluetoothGatt requires a Context that the Swift initialiser never carried; the Activity layer must assign TeslaVehicle.applicationContext before start().
BluetoothGatt allows one outstanding write, so the 20-byte blocks are queued in pendingWriteBlocks and drained in onCharacteristicWrite instead of being written back to back.
